He said: “I think we’ve preferred at the end to have the best players, probably, than a player that maybe is specifically for that [right-sided] position. I’m very used from my previous teams to demand for all the wingers to play both sides.

“Probably all of them have played more on the left, but I would say I’ve seen them in a good place on the right. Probably Rio is more specific from the left side, but I think he has also showed the willingness to improve and play on the right. Even Bradley, he’s very open and I think he can play right and left. He started actually more on the right side when he started with Olympique Lyonnais. I’m happy with the four wingers we have and I’m sure we are going to be able to cover those two positions.”

Sports.title: World Cup wishlists, early movers, big clearouts: 2026 summer transfer window trends
Sports.content:
On the World Cup wishlist …

The World Cup is always a good shop window. Yan Diomande was already a rising star at RB Leipzig but shining for Côte d’Ivoire in the US helped push up his price tag before a £115.7m move to Real Madrid. There were other breakout stars: Switzerland’s Johan Manzambi, whose signature Aston Villa pipped Newcastle to; Bosnia and Herzegovina’s Kerim Alajbegovic, who went to Juventus; and Ghana’s Caleb Yirenkyi, who is now in the Premier League with Coventry. Cape Verde’s cult hero Vozinha now keeps net for the Chilean giants Colo-Colo and Morocco’s attacking dynamo, Ismael Saibari, has rocked up at Bayern. Billy Munday

Time is of the essence

While Europe’s wealthiest clubs generally allowed the World Cup to run its course before moving for their main targets, there were some exceptions. Real Madrid announced the signing of Marc Cucurella for £52m as he was getting ready to start Spain’s opener against Cape Verde, then Bernardo Silva before Portugal began their campaign two days later. Liverpool spent heavily early on as they signed Víctor Muñoz for £34.5m in mid-June and completed their pre-agreed £60m deal for Jérémy Jacquet at the start of July. Tottenham had spent almost £230m on Jan Paul van Hecke, Mateus Fernandes and Sandro Tonali before the last 16 was over, also adding Andy Robertson and Marcos Senesi on free transfers. Other clubs seemed to treat the World Cup as an opportunity to do deals under the radar. Bayer Leverkusen moved quickly, just as they did in January, to sign promising youngsters in Kennet Eichhorn and Afonso Moreira for a combined £32.8m in June. Brighton were among the most proactive squad builders in the Premier League, spending just over £50m on Zadok Yohanna, Costinha and Pascal Struijk before the World Cup action had moved beyond the last 32. Will Magee

View image in fullscreen Zadok Yohanna was an early arrival for Brighton, who did not wait around to make signings. Photograph: Toby Melville/Reuters

Premier League newcomers splash the cash

“Think about us like a volcano,” Hull’s owner, Acun Ilicali, said in July. “It’s boiling right now and it’s going to erupt.” He was not wrong. In the end, the promoted Premier League side signed 18 players this summer for a combined sum of £156.5m. Ipswich went even further, splashing £194.7m on 15 additions, while Coventry spent £122.4m on 11 new signings. It is a far cry from a few years ago when many promoted teams were frugal, often relying on the players who took them to the promised land. As recently as 2021 the three promoted teams, Norwich, Watford and Brentford, spent a combined £98.8m – with the latter’s acquisition of Kristoffer Ajer from Celtic the most expensive signing at £13m. The fact that Premier League newcomers are spending so lavishly is a reminder of the division’s financial dominance and the game’s increasingly extreme economic disparities. Marcus Christenson

French talent factory ups its output

In sharp contrast to the Premier League, where eight clubs had a net spend over £100m and only six made a net gain, 15 out of 18 Ligue 1 clubs made money on player trading this summer. Paris Saint-Germain led the way thanks in no small part to the £123m deal which took Bradley Barcola to Liverpool, making a net profit of more than £150m overall. Lille, who made around £100m, sanctioned big-money departures for Ayyoub Bouaddi and Matias Fernandez-Pardo, who joined Manchester City and Newcastle for £85.7m and £51m respectively. Strasbourg, the smaller cog in BlueCo’s transfer machine, brought in almost £90m as they moved on Diego Moreira, Julio Enciso, Abdoul Ouattara, Guéla Doué, Valentín Barco and Emmanuel Emegha – the latter two moving to, that’s right, Chelsea. While Ligue 1 has been a conveyor belt of talent for some time, its output is reaching new levels. Of the 15 biggest fees ever received by French clubs, five have come in this window. WM

View image in fullscreen Bradley Barcola was the most expensive of numerous acquisitions from Ligue 1 clubs. Photograph: Liverpool FC/Getty Images

Fiorentina lead clubs in clearout mode

There has been plenty of upheaval this summer, but nowhere more so than at Fiorentina. After battling relegation for much of last season, eventually finishing 15th in Serie A, the Viola have moved on 34 players either permanently or on loan, with Moise Kean and Tariq Lamptey among the high-profile departees. No other club in Europe’s “big five” leagues can match that but Chelsea, with 33 leavers (18 on loan), are not far off. While Chelsea made a net profit of around £60m thanks to the £125m deadline-day deal for Enzo Fernández, Fiorentina have spent more than £100m net on a rebuild from the ground up. Depending on interpretation, that’s either a sign of Premier League money taking on a bizarre and irrational life of its own, or a lesson in the eye-watering cost of fixing a failed recruitment strategy. WM

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Inter order the full English

There has been a steady stream of English players heading to Italy in recent years, but it’s not often three turn up at one club in quick succession. Inter have opened the floodgates this summer, signing John Stones from Manchester City on a free, Djed Spence from Tottenham for £25.6m and Curtis Jones from Liverpool for £25.7m. The pantheon of Inter cult heroes includes Paul Ince and Ashley Young, who won the Scudetto in 2021, so the club has a longstanding Anglophile streak, but Serie A has also become an increasingly attractive destination. With Omari Hutchinson joining Fikayo Tomori and Ruben Loftus-Cheek at Milan, the derby will have a distinctly English flavour. WM

View image in fullscreen Curtis Jones savours victory against Cagliari on his Inter debut. Photograph: Mattia Pistoia/Inter/Getty Images

It is Ireland v Scotland in the frontlines of Seville this season. Perhaps inspired by their pre-season trip to Dublin, Real Betis spent £17.1m to sign Troy Parrott from AZ, where he scored 31 goals in the Netherlands last season. Manuel Pellegrini said moving to La Liga is a “leap” for Parrott, but it’s not as big a jump as Robbie Ure has made. The £5.6m Glasgow-born striker, uncapped by Scotland, has become Sevilla’s new No 9 off the back of 15 goals in 15 games in the first half of the Swedish season for the unlikely Allsvenskan leaders, Sirius. “I wanted to be in top-class environments,” the 22-year-old said. BM

Transfer tumbleweed and tight pockets

They may have been the least active club in Europe’s top leagues this summer with zero new arrivals but, given their tradition of only signing players born or trained in the Basque Country, Athletic Bilbao have a good excuse. Marseille, not so much. Other than fulfilling their pre-agreed obligations to buy Timothy Weah and Hamed Traorè, OM have not brought in a single player while stripping their squad back to the bare bones in a drastic attempt to repair their finances. Then there are the clubs with modest budgets who have opted for a thrifty approach. Málaga, newly promoted to La Liga, have brought in seven players but not paid a single transfer fee. Le Mans, new arrivals in Ligue 1, have limited themselves to two undisclosed fees while making nine signings, also allowing five players to leave without receiving a fee in return. WM

Sports.title: Daniel Kretinsky to become biggest West Ham shareholder in blow to Amanda Staveley
Sports.content:
Daniel Kretinsky is set to become the biggest shareholder at West Ham after striking an agreement with David Sullivan, dealing a blow to Amanda Staveley’s hopes of buying a stake in the Championship club.

Staveley was a guest at the London Stadium for West Ham’s 4-2 win over Wolves earlier this week and was pushing to buy Vanessa Gold’s 25.1% stake in the club. The British businesswoman, previously a director at Newcastle, had struck a deal with the Gold family in July and was fronting a consortium looking for a way on to the east London club’s board.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

However that arrangement sparked a process allowing West Ham’s other shareholders to exercise their pre-emption rights over the Gold family’s stake before a 5.30pm deadline on Thursday evening. It is believed that Kretinsky, a Czech billionaire and the owner of Royal Mail, and Sullivan have come to an agreement that will see the former increase his 27% stake to 46%. Sources have said there is unlikely to be a way back for Staveley’s group.

Sources have consistently said that Kretinsky, who will surpass Sullivan as the biggest shareholder, is determined to increase his interest in West Ham as they look to rebuild after their relegation from the Premier League last season. His plans were complicated by Staveley entering the picture.

However it is understood that Sullivan rebuffed an inquiry from Staveley about buying his stake during the summer. The 77-year-old privately indicated a preference to deal with Kretinsky, who first bought a stake in West Ham in November 2021. The arrangement will see Sullivan increase his stake from 38.8% to 40%, making him the second largest shareholder. The American businessman Tripp Smith’s stake will go from 8% to 11% and the remaining shareholders will rise from 1.1% to 3%. Staveley would need shareholders not to take up their pre-emption rights to have a chance of making a separate offer for the Gold shares.

Sullivan stepped down as a director and co-chair of West Ham in June, before a joint investigation by the Times and Panorama reporting on seven women abusing his power and preying on them for sex in claims that date back to the 1980s and 90s. The 77-year-old categorically denies the allegations. Sullivan has been present at West Ham’s home games this season but does not have a seat on the board and is no longer the most powerful person at the club.

Sports.title: Thierry Henry says players ‘have more power than they think’ amid Fifa scandals
Sports.content:
As Fifa continues to face scrutiny from some confederations and fans, Thierry Henry has encouraged players to use their voice as the political battle for control of international soccer unfolds. The former Arsenal and Barcelona forward turned pundit spoke with the Guardian on Tuesday alongside Kate Scott and Jamie Carragher as CBS and Paramount prepare for this season’s Champions League broadcasts.

“For me, the players have more power than they think they have,” Henry said when asked for his thoughts on the situation. “And if they want it to change, they can make it happen – especially nowadays.”

Fifa has been under public duress in the wake of multiple scandals surrounding the 2026 World Cup, exacerbated further after reports of Gianni Infantino’s effort to sell the World Cup’s commercial rights. The ensuing month has seen the Fifa president face significant criticism, with Uefa exploring potential legal options against Infantino.

Scott, who anchors the CBS panel comprising Henry, Carragher and Micah Richards, spoke extensively about 2021’s attempted Super League project and the ensuing debacle in an Apple TV documentary. The Super League saga seemed to pit the business interests of the sport’s business class against the game’s heart, represented by players, coaches and fans. The latest situation involving Fifa has progressed in a similar spirit.

“I think it’s going to be really interesting to see [what comes next],” Scott said. “I think probably a large portion of world football has come to a point where they would like to see a change in [the Fifa presidency], similarly to the way we felt about [the Super League] … I think if you’re invested in the game and you love the game, it just kind of leaves a bad taste.”

Infantino has been re-elected twice since 2016, both times without a challenger. The next vote is slated for 18 March 2027, with no alternative having declared their candidacy.

“I have no idea which way that will go, because obviously one thing that Gianni Infantino has proven to be within world football is a very smart power broker and has understood how to make allies, use those allies to his benefit,” Scott said.

For Henry, though, the voice of the players can – and should – be a bigger part of the conversation.

“Players have all the power if they want to, and sometimes they don’t, I think, use it or realize actually the power that they have,” Henry said. “You guys in the US know fully well: when the player wants to do something, the league listens. You saw it with the NBA. You saw it with the NFL … At one point, the players are always on the side: go entertain, take your money, leave.

“Us debating about it here, what’s going to change? We can all have a view whether it’s a good one or a bad one … But for me, the players have more power than they think they have. And if they want it to change, they can make it happen – especially nowadays.”

Sports.title: Manchester City’s Vivianne Miedema could miss rest of year with knee injury
Sports.content:
Manchester City could be without Vivianne Miedema for at least the rest of 2026, the Guardian understands, after the Netherlands forward sustained a knee injury.

According to multiple sources the injury is not an anterior cruciate ligament but is serious and there are fears she will not return until after the Women’s Super League’s winter break. A statement from the club on Tuesday said Miedema would miss the “start of the season”.

City are understood to have sought reinforcements in attacking midfield to cover for Miedema, who predominantly played as a No 10 for the WSL champions last term. The Paris Saint-Germain and Nigeria midfielder Jennifer Echegini and the Everton and Spain forward Ornella Vignola are players City are understood to have inquired about before the 11pm BST WSL transfer deadline. According to sources, PSG are not willing to sell Echegini.

Arsenal have signed the France defender Élisa De Almeida from PSG, for a fee understood to be just over £500,000. The 28-year-old, who made 154 appearances since 2021 for PSG and has 52 caps for France, has been given Arsenal’s No 5 shirt.



De Almeida is an experienced centre-back and was part of France’s Euro 2025 and 2023 World Cup squads. Arsenal are understood to need centre-back cover partly because their defender Katie Reid’s recovery from the anterior cruciate ligament injury sustained last November is being managed carefully, meaning the 19-year-old is not expected to be available before November.



The Arsenal head coach Renée Slegers told the club’s website: “We’re very pleased to add Élisa to our squad. Her composure, mobility and experience are all strengths in her game and I look forward to working with her on the training pitch.”

The summer window has been another record-breaking one for the women’s game globally. The latest mid-year snapshot report released by Fifa on Thursday showed global spending on international women’s transfer fees this summer had surpassed $28m (£20.7m), more than double last summer’s $12.3m. In 2022 it was $1.23m. English clubs led the spending this summer with $8m, followed by Spain ($6.6m) and Germany ($4.9m).

West Ham are understood to be set to sign the Japan legend Saki Kumagai from London City Lionesses, with personal terms having been agreed a few hours before the deadline.

Manchester City have signed the England goalkeeper Anna Moorhouse on loan from Orlando Pride until the end of January 2027.

The 31-year-old, who has been capped twice by the Lionesses, told City’s media channels: “I’m happy to be here with the champions of England. When a club like Manchester City calls, you have to answer.”

The promoted side Crystal Palace made a deadline-day signing with the return of Shanade Hopcroft. The 28-year-old former Chelsea academy player, who helped Palace win promotion in 2023-24, has signed a two-year deal.

The WSL season gets under way on Friday when London City Lionesses host Manchester United. The new United head coach, Eva Olid, said on Thursday her team would not add more signings. United secured the Mexico midfielder Rebeca Bernal, who can also play at centre-back, on Wednesday, and Olid said at her first press conference since replacing Marc Skinner that Bernal would be available for Friday’s match.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

View image in fullscreen Manchester United’s head coach, Eva Olid, said: ‘It was not about signing players quick. It is about signing the right players.’ Photograph: Poppy Townson/MUFC/Manchester United/Getty Images

Olid, the former Hearts manager, is promising to bring “attacking football” to United. She used the word “attacking” eight times during her 17-minute press conference and spoke of her enthusiasm for developing young players. She said of her attacking style: “They appointed me for that reason. I have to go with that. We will be brave in attack, trying to play that attractive football. Our main focus [is] that attacking mentality. We want to play with the ball, a nice football, create a lot of chances.”

On waiting until January before adding more players, Olid said: “The players I need are different from the players the previous manager needed. [It has been a] short period to react. We have some plans in January about signing players that I really need for my style of play. It was not about signing players quick. It is about signing the right players.”

Olid was also asked about United’s investment in the women’s game, with Chelsea spending nearly three times as much as them on their women’s team wage bill in the most recent set of published accounts. Olid spoke positively about her club’s backing, saying: “The message has always been about: ‘We want to invest in everything.’ As I said, not just on players. Because I think it is important we have the right staff, the right coaches … The message is that they want to win. They want to win. I think I am here to make that happen, but with a solid identity.”

Arturo Ruiz, who was appointed as Brighton’s head coach on 28 August, acknowledged at his first press conference that he had not had much time with his players but said: “We need to be patient and put the focus on high-performance, and results will come. If that [happens] soon, it’s better, but if not, we need to be very clear in our gameplans.”

The 29-year-old former Real Sociedad head coach added: “Our style of play will be very adaptable without the ball, very aggressive when we need to [be], very compact when we need to be as well, and defending the box really well. With the ball, we are going to be a very dynamic team with a clear identity.” Brighton host Arsenal on Sunday.

Sports.title: The WSL returns bigger than ever and with a mouthwatering title race
Sports.content:
It has been a summer of change for women’s football in England, with expansion of the Women’s Super League to 14 teams bringing three new sides into the fold, huge transfers hitting the headlines, changes to the League Cup and a new name on the WSL trophy as we prepare for kick-off on Friday.

Players have had a proper break over the summer, with no major international women’s tournament for the first time in six years (Covid delays pushed back the Tokyo Olympics to 2021 and the European Championship to 2022, followed by the 2023 World Cup, 2024 Paris Olympics and Euro 2025). As a result, managers have had a full pre-season with all available players for the first time in more than half a decade too.

In many respects, this is the most mouthwatering and unpredictable WSL season of recent years. At the top end, the title race is wide open from the outset. The holders, Manchester City, have perhaps the most settled squad and a potent attack spearheaded by the winner of three back-to-back Golden Boots, Bunny Shaw. However, they will also be juggling their league and FA Cup title defences alongside Champions League football, which they avoided last season through a fourth-place finish in the league the preceding year. That will be counteracted somewhat by Champions League teams no longer competing in the rebranded League Cup, which also opens the door to domestic silverware for those outside the top three.

Arsenal and Renée Slegers have no excuses for a poor season, after two disappointing and costly starts to WSL campaigns were somewhat understandable due to the tight turnarounds following the major tournament exploits of many players and Champions League qualifying campaigns in the 2022-23 and 2023-24 season. The Gunners have overhauled their squad in the summer and lowered the age profile, adding experienced top-level talent such as Georgia Stanway, Ona Batlle, Géraldine Reuteler and Selina Cerci.

Chelsea have embarked on their own squad evolution, after a transitional season where they sought to strike the balance between making changes and retaining that winning spirit synonymous with the side. Some hugely influential and longstanding players have departed in Millie Bright, who has retired, Guro Reiten, Sam Kerr, Catarina Macario, Johanna Rytting Kaneryd and Niamh Charles.

Melvine Malard, who has reunited with Sonia Bompastor having played under her at OL Lyonnes, has already hit the ground running with two goals from the bench in the team’s 5-2 win against Real Sociedad in the first leg of their Champions League qualifier. Where playing in Champions League qualifiers was a burden in seasons after major international tournaments, this campaign it could be an advantage for the Blues who have a chance to shake off any rust before they kick off their title challenge.

It perhaps feels a little unfair to drop Manchester United out of the title challengers and to place them in with “the best of the rest” but, with a nine-point gap between them and Chelsea last season, a lack of serious backing from the club and a so far underwhelming transfer window, this season could be a tough one for them.

Marc Skinner’s exit after a frustrating five years in Manchester was welcomed by sections of their fanbase but the manager arguably helped the side to punch well above their weight, with a comparatively small wage bill despite a competitive turnover. Eva Olid is an exciting young manager, having led Hearts from the bottom of the Scottish Women’s Premier League (with the team avoiding relegation only because of league expansion) to the title before her departure at the end of last season. However, if fans are hoping for a fresh start they should perhaps temper their excitement, with the club leaning into Olid’s reputation for player development and their four summer recruits so far not doing anywhere near enough to offset the loss of their outgoing players.

View image in fullscreen Eva Olid talks to the media on the eve of the new WSL season. Photograph: Poppy Townson/MUFC/Manchester United/Getty Images

They could be troubled by a chasing pack who have invested shrewdly, in the case of Tottenham, Everton, Liverpool and Brighton, or boldly, in the case of London City Lionesses.

United’s first challenge is against Michele Kang’s big-spending side as they open the WSL season on Friday night, when the two-time Ballon d’Or winner Alexia Putellas will answer the question of whether she can “do it on a Friday night in Bromley”.

The London City manager, Eder Maestre, has the enviable job of being able to put together his dream team, but the unenviable task of trying to gel a side that have had 13 departures and eight players coming in. The decision to remove the manager that led them into the WSL, Jocelyn Prêcheur, was billed as a purely football one by sources, with the club sixth in the table in their first season in the top flight. That decision, though, shows Kang will not accept mediocrity and the patience required by Maestre may not be forthcoming.

Tottenham and Brighton are two other teams aiming high. Martin Ho’s Spurs are the league’s not-so-dark dark horses, with a hugely impressive debut season for their manager followed by an astute and targeted transfer window, which has included the recruitment of the third-highest scorer in the league last season, the midfielder Kirsty Hanson, and the club-record signing Alice Sombath from OL Lyonnes.

The impact of the shock departure of Dario Vidosic from Brighton, with his move to the NWSL side Angel City announced soon after, will be fully known when the season gets under way, but they have recruited a very promising young replacement, Arturo Ruiz, and their squad has huge potential after a strong window.

Everton, Liverpool and West Ham all have potential to be surprise packages this season after similarly impressive transfer windows as the middle to lower end of the table ups its game.

View image in fullscreen Everton will be looking to make an impact in the top half this season. Photograph: Tony Smith/Alamy

Aston Villa have recruited 10 to replace the nine departed players but the fear will be that the incoming players struggle to fill the hole left by players such as Hanson, Ebony Salmon and Gabi Nunes.

Of the newcomers to the WSL, Birmingham and Crystal Palace have overseen similarly large squad turnovers, with some top-level talent brought in to attempt to ensure they avoid the drop back down to WSL 2 such as Millie Turner and Lisa Naalsund for the former and Bethany England for the latter.

Charlton have not been able to recruit so ambitiously in the summer, though eight new players have arrived to help the manager, Karen Hills, and her side who hope to leave egg on the faces of many who have put them as favourites to go down.

Predicting results or the outcome of the season is nigh- on impossible though, and that will be the hope: that the expanded league delivers surprises.

Sports.title: Taylor Harwood-Bellis left out of Champions League squad just days after joining Aston Villa
Sports.content:
Taylor Harwood-Bellis left out of Champions League squad just days after joining Aston Villa

Aston Villa have named their squad for the Champions League league phase, but Taylor Harwood-Bellis was not included.

The decision has come only days after the centre-back completed his summer move from Southampton.



2 Harwood-Bellis has missed out on Villa's league phase squad Credit: Getty

Harwood-Bellis put pen to paper in a deal worth an initial £25million, with another £5m in add-ons also included.

However, he will not play in the opening stage of their Champions League campaign.

Also omitted from the squad was centre-back Modou Keba Cisse and teenage striker Brian Madjo, who scored for Villa against Paris Saint-Germain in the Super Cup.



As listed on the UEFA website, 23 players have been selected for Villa's league phase matches.

Their squad includes nine of their signings from the summer window, which closed on Tuesday night.



Zion Suzuki, Matteo Ruggeri, Aaron Wan-Bissaka, Leon Goretzka, Joao Gomes, Johan Manzambi, Nicolas Jackson, Alejandro Garnacho and Ibrahim Mbaye are all available for selection.

Could Harwood-Bellis still play in the Champions League?

Although he cannot feature during the league phase, Harwood-Bellis could still play later on in the competition.



Clubs who qualify for the knockout stages can register a maximum of three new players in their primary List A.

However, the squad must still have a maximum of 25 players in total.

Harwood-Bellis could even find himself involved in Villa's plans during the league phase.

2 Emery has selected his squad for this season's competition Credit: Getty

An outfield player named on List A can be replaced should they suffer a long-term injury or illness that lasts at least 60 days.



Clubs can temporarily replace just one outfield player and bring in a new one from the first match up to and including the sixth.

This means that, if one of Villa's selected centre-backs was ruled out for 60 or more days, then Harwood-Bellis could replace them.

Who will Villa play in the Champions League?

The league phase draw was conducted on August 27, with Unai Emery and his side learning their eight opponents.

Villa first travel to Club Brugge before back-to-back home matches against Fenerbahce and Viking FK.



Tough tests at Galatasaray and Barcelona follow, and then reigning champions Paris Saint-Germain are their final test of 2026.

Borussia Dortmund and Slavia Prague cap off their league phase, where a top-eight finish would send them into the knockouts.

Sports.title: Will Enzo Fernandez start for Man City immediately after £125m Chelsea transfer?
Sports.content:
Enzo Fernandez is the joint most expensive player in British football history after his mega-money move from Chelsea to Manchester City.

And the £125m midfielder will be itching to make his debut for his new club.

2 Fernandez has been reunited with his old Chelsea boss Enzo Maresca at Man City Credit: AFP

Man City, who have won their first two Premier League games under Enzo Maresca, are back in action at home to Coventry on Saturday.

Will Fernandez start for Man City against Coventry?

Following the summer arrivals of Elliot Anderson and Ayyoub Bouaddi – also for substantial fees – City certainly have no shortage of quality options in midfield.

Anderson started the wins over Bournemouth and Crystal Palace, with Bouaddi replacing him from the bench for his debut late on in the latter game.

And while 18-year-old Bouaddi is undoubtedly one of the most prodigious midfield talents around, Maresca may feel a need to ease him into the rigours of the Premier League.

Fernandez, by contrast, has been there and done it, spending the last three-and-a-half years with Chelsea.

He's also got some minutes in the tank already this term, making what proved to be his final appearance for the Blues as a substitute in their opening-weekend win at Fulham.

As such, one would expect him to be in contention to start for City this weekend.

That could be bad news for Nico O'Reilly, who started in a more advanced midfield role against Bournemouth before playing deeper against Palace.

And with Josko Gvardiol starting the campaign so well in the England international's slightly more natural left-back role, scoring the winner against Bournemouth and providing an assist last time out, O'Reilly may have to make do with a spot on the bench for the visit of Coventry.

Will City's other new signings play?

City have made two other signings since their last outing, both wingers.

2 City won the race to sign Ndiaye Credit: Getty

Brazilian Allan joined from Palmeiras on the penultimate day of the transfer window, with Iliman Ndiaye arriving from Everton on deadline day.

But neither is likely to dislodge Phil Foden or Antoine Semenyo – both of whom set up goals in the 4-1 victory over Palace – so will probably find themselves among the substitutes in the first instance.

What has Enzo Fernandez said?

Speaking after completing his switch to City, Fernandez expressed his desire to go to another level. He said: "I could not be happier to be here, and I am ready for the challenge of helping City continue winning trophies. This is a club built for success.

"If you look across the squad, City have quality in every area. I want to learn from my new teammates and become a better player.

"I pride myself on continually improving my game. Anyone who’s worked with me will know how hard I train every single day and how much I put into matches. I give absolutely everything and I can promise Manchester City that will continue now I’m here."

What have City fans said?

The signing of Fernandez has divided opinion among City fans following his antics for Argentina at the World Cup.

But one supporter who's certainly excited to have him onboard is Noel Gallagher, who told talkSPORT he admired Fernandez's 'ballsy' nature.

Sports.title: Viktor Gyokeres told he is ‘lucky’ to be at Arsenal just one year after £64m transfer
Sports.content:
Viktor Gyokeres told he is ‘lucky’ to be at Arsenal just one year after £64m transfer

Troy Deeney believes Viktor Gyokeres considers himself fortunate to remain an Arsenal player now the transfer window has closed.

The striker was linked with a summer exit just a year after becoming a Gunner with his £63.7million move from Sporting.



2 Gyokeres has not played a single minute in the league this season Credit: Getty

Atletico Madrid forward Julian Alvarez became a dream target for the Premier League champions amid fellow interest from Barcelona.

talkSPORT reported that, to supplement a potential deal, Arsenal explored the possibility of offering Gyokeres during their initial talks.

Alvarez did not sign for the Gunners and, therefore, Gyokeres did not leave, with Mikel Arteta insisting that he would remain at the club.



However, the Sweden international has not featured in either of their Premier League victories against Coventry City and Aston Villa.

Kai Havertz has been the preferred option up top so, with Gyokeres struggling for minutes, Deeney senses he has had some fortune.



"I think he knows he's lucky to be there, personally," he said on the Premier League All Access podcast for talkSPORT.

"I think when you look at his career, look at his attributes, he's probably going, 'I'm at a team here, I've won the Premier League, this is unbelievable'.



"He will be used in the Champions League, but also there's a business element to this where sometimes, things just get swept under the rug now.

"He'll have a conversation, I wouldn't be surprised if we start seeing over the next two, three weeks, he gets more minutes and more time now the window's closed.

"Mikel is not stupid enough to just keep him on the outside, he'll be like, 'Alright, you're still here, you're part of the squad, let's move forward.'"

2 Havertz sits top of the pecking order at Arsenal Credit: Getty



Could Gyokeres play for Arsenal against Chelsea?

After being an unused substitute in the wins over Coventry and Villa, Gyokeres is waiting for his first league appearance.

Havertz was quiet at Villa Park as he managed just one shot, but he is likely to return to the starting XI this weekend.

Arsenal host Chelsea in the headline Premier League clash on Sunday, with both sides having a 100 per cent record thus far.

Gyokeres looks set to be named on the bench for a third consecutive match, but could earn his first outing.



Now that Gabriel Jesus has left for Barcelona, the 28-year-old joins Havertz as the only striker options at Arsenal.

Sports.title: Jadon Sancho handed Jesse Lingard warning amid ‘fascinating’ free transfer links
Sports.content:
Jadon's Sancho's rumoured move to Brazilian club Palmeiras would be 'fascinating' were it to come to fruition.

That's the view of South American football expert Tim Vickery, with Sancho linked with a surprise switch to the three-time Copa Libertadores winners.

2 Sancho's last appearance for Manchester United came in the 2024 Community Shield Credit: Getty

The winger is a free agent after leaving Manchester United at the end of his contract this summer.

And should he head to Brazil, he'll follow in the footsteps of former United teammate Jesse Lingard, who joined Corinthians back in March.

Vickery keen on Sancho to Palmeiras

However, Vickery stressed that it wouldn't be the same kind of move – with Lingard now 33 and Sancho, at 26, still theoretically in his prime.

He told talkSPORT's Hawksbee and Jacobs: "They've [Palmeiras] got a week to sort this one out [the Brazilian transfer window closes next Friday, September 11].

"Jesse Lingard is over here with Corinthians. He's not done very much; he's not getting a game. But obviously Jadon Sancho is at a very different stage in his career.

"They've just sold Allan to Man City, picked up one or two injuries…it would be fascinating, it really would. I'm hoping it happens.

"They're in three competitions. Top of the Brazilian league, quarter-finals of the Libertadores, semi-finals of the Brazilian Cup.

"There's loads and loads to play for, so he can keep himself in the international shop window coming over on a short-term deal.

"Bring it on – I'd love to see it happen."

Sancho's United nightmare

Sancho joined Man United from Borussia Dortmund for £73m in 2021 but failed to live up to his price tag.

2 Sancho signed for Man United when Ole Gunnar Solskjaer was manager Credit: Getty

After two unconvincing seasons with Old Trafford, during which he dropped out of the England squad, he was loaned back to Dortmund in 2023.

Further loan spells with Chelsea and Aston Villa followed, but Sancho looked a shadow of the player he was during his breakthrough years in the Bundesliga.

A move to Brazil would be a left-field one, but it could be just what he needs to kickstart his career – away from the glaring limelight of the European game.

Trailblazing Lingard

Lingard became the first Englishman to play in the Brazilian top flight when he arrived after leaving South Korea's FC Seoul at the end of last year.

He is, however, one of a number of European players currently plying their trade in the Brasileirao.

They include another of Lingard's former United colleagues, Netherlands striker Memphis Depay, who has been at Corinthians since 2024, and ex-Chelsea and Spain midfielder Saul of Flamengo.

Sports.title: Estevao ‘impatient’ as Chelsea’s £160m best friend duo send Brazilian star down pecking order
Sports.content:
Estevao ‘impatient’ as Chelsea’s £160m best friend duo send Brazilian star down pecking order

Estevao Willian could be growing impatient at Chelsea following the signing of fellow attacker Morgan Rogers.

That's according to Tim Vickery, with the Brazilian starlet facing new competition in his second season at Stamford Bridge.



3 It's not been an easy start for Estevao at Chelsea this season Credit: Getty

After officially arriving from Palmeiras last summer, Estevao delivered a hugely impressive debut campaign in English football at Chelsea.

He played 36 times, scored eight goals and assisted four others as he turned into one of the most exciting Premier League prospects.

A hamstring injury ended his season early and he missed out on the World Cup with Brazil having looked set to be named in their squad.



Over the summer, Chelsea made the club-record £117million signing of Rogers, who is best friends with his England co-star Cole Palmer.

The duo started in their league wins over Fulham and Brighton, as well as the Carabao Cup victory against Luton Town.



Estevao on the other hand has earned just one start and, although it is still early in the season, the 19-year-old may just be slightly restless.

Has Estevao become 'impatient' at Chelsea?

Speaking to talkSPORT, South American football journalist Vickery addressed the potential unhappiness and said: "He chose Chelsea.



"It's the first real, genuine, Brazilian superstar to choose Chelsea over the likes of Real Madrid and Barcelona.

"Maybe he just feels that he's fallen a little bit down the pecking order with Morgan Rogers, who is Cole Palmer's great mate, coming in.

"So, maybe there's a little bit of impatience there, we will find out.

3 Palmer and Rogers have become a go-to attacking pair at Chelsea Credit: Getty



"It is a shame because he gave us some fantastic (performances)... the injury is unfortunate, because I wonder what he might have done at the World Cup because (Carlo) Ancelotti loves him.

"Running into that injury was a little bit unfortunate, but it's doubly unfortunate for me if Chelsea can't give him a regular gig because I think he's just a fantastic talent."

Rogers and Palmer success this season

With both players academy graduates at Manchester City, Rogers and Palmer reunited at club level when the former signed for Chelsea.

They made an excellent start to the season in the 3-2 win at Fulham as each player found the target, whilst Palmer also bagged an assist.



Rogers provided for Pedro Neto in the 4-3 triumph against Brighton, whilst his long-term friend scored a second.

It was a quiet night at the office for the pair when they hosted Luton.

3 Estevao will hope for more regular minutes as the season progresses Credit: Getty

Instead, it was Estevao who impressed for Xabi Alonso's side as his shot went off Hakeem Odoffin for an own-goal during the 2-0 win.



Alonso is likely to stick with Rogers and Palmer playing alongside the in-form Joao Pedro when they visit Arsenal on Sunday.

Sports.title: Chelsea announce signing of Brazilian prodigy 48 hours after transfer window shuts
Sports.content:
Chelsea have confirmed the signing of 18-year-old Brazilian full-back Denner from Corinthians.

Denner, who starred for Corinthians' Under-20 side, has signed an eight-year deal with the Blues.

2 Denner will link up with Chelsea's age-group squads at their Cobham training base Credit: Getty

The teenager will link up with Cobham Next Gen (CNG), Chelsea's newly rebranded Under-19 and Under-21 squads.

Denner's rapid rise

Denner joined the youth set-up of hometown club Corinthians at the age of 13.

By 16, he was representing them at U-20 level, helping that team finish as runners-up in the Sao Paulo Youth Cup.

He scored the opening goal in the final as Corinthians were beaten by Sao Paulo.

Chelsea reportedly first agreed a deal for Denner back in 2025 with a view to signing him this year.

He's one of three academy signings the Blues have made this summer, following midfielder Harrison Bettoni from Wigan and defender Alfie Osborne from Hearts.

An attack-minded full-back whose naturally position is on the left, Denner has played for Brazil up to Under-17 level.

He was part of the squad that won the 2025 South American Under-17 Championship.

According to Brazilian media, Denner is a cousin of Arsenal star Gabriel.

And if he follows anything like the career trajectory of the Premier League title-winning Gunners centre-back, Chelsea have a very special talent indeed on their hands.

2 Gabriel may come up against a family member in the next few years Credit: Getty

Chelsea's lucrative window

This summer's transfer window was another hugely busy one for Chelsea.

As well as spending over £300m to bring in players such as Moran Rogers and Maxence Lacroix, the Blues made around £400m in player sales.

A substantial chunk of their total income came from the sale of Enzo Fernandez alone.

The midfielder joined Manchester City on deadline day for £125m.

That fee equalled the record in British football paid by Liverpool to sign Alexander Isak from Newcastle last year.

Tosin Adarabioyo and Marc Guiu also made deadline-day moves away from Stamford Bridge, heading to Tottenham and RB Leipzig respectively.

Sports.title: ‘Toothless’ Premier League side warned of relegation threat after ‘uninspiring’ transfer window
Sports.content:
Fulham are heading towards Premier League relegation and showed a lack of motivation in the summer transfer window.

That's the view of talkSPORT host Max Scott as the west London side bemoan a worrying start to the season with two defeats in two.



4 Fulham could be battling for Premier League survival this season Credit: Getty

After a 3-2 home loss to local rivals Chelsea, Sunderland beat Fulham 1-0 on Sunday to ensure they remain without a point in the league.

With Liverpool and Manchester United two of their upcoming tests, new boss Alvaro Arbeloa faces an uphill climb at Craven Cottage.

But, even with 36 more games to play this season, Scott can only see one outcome for the Cottagers - relegation to the Championship.



Speaking on NO BS for talkSPORT, he explained why he tipped Fulham to finish in the bottom three of the Premier League amid their poor start.

"We're going to talk about Sunderland v Fulham," Scott said.

"For me, it was a relegation six-pointer. I have backed Hull, Sunderland and Fulham to go down.



"I'm questioning Hull, I'm not so sure about Sunderland, I still think they're going to be down there. Fulham? They're absolute goners."

Co-host Olly Clink labelled the Cottagers 'terrible' as Scott continued: "Limp-wristed, and no wonder Arbeloa has already lost his rag in his post-match comments after the game.



"I just think... I know this sounds harsh, but what are Fulham?"

Do Fulham regret losing Marco Silva?

Scott once again tipped Fulham for the drop, and then questioned why the club didn't do enough to keep former manager Silva.

4 Arbeloa is winless in the Premier League Credit: Getty

4 Fulham may be left to rue letting Silva leave Credit: Getty

The Portuguese left at the end of last season amid the expiration of his contract in June and is now at Benfica, where has won six of his nine games in charge.



Arbeloa replaced him following a spell at Real Madrid, but it's his predecessor who Scott believes that Fulham should have backed.

Max Scott labels Fulham a 'waste of space'

"Just toothless," Scott said.

"I think, what are they doing not throwing the money at Marco Silva? They have a lot of money in the bank, their owner (Shahid Khan) does. Their stadium, the amount of money they charge Fulham fans...

"They're a waste of space. Give it to Birmingham, give it to Wrexham, that spot, give it to a big club like Sheffield Wednesday in a couple of years if they can get there.

"I just think Fulham are a bit boring. I would never tune into a Fulham game, because Fulham are playing. I would tune into watch Forest play them... I'm just a bit bored of them.



Fulham signings in summer 2026 Gonzalo Garcia - £34m, Real Madrid Shea Charles - £30m, Southampton David Affengruber - £8.6m, Elche Cesar Palacios - £8m, Real Madrid Jonah Kusi-Asare - £5m, Bayern Munich Manuel Angel - £3m, Real Madrid Hugo Larsson - Loan, Eintracht Frankfurt

4 Arbeloa has Fulham sitting 16th in the table Credit: Getty

"And their window has been so uninspiring as well."

"It's a lovely ground," he added. "I've heard from a few players that they really like playing at Fulham, because you don't get the pressure.

"But sometimes, pressure creates diamonds, and there's no diamonds at Fulham at the minute.

"I think they miss the edge that Marco Silva brings, I think they failed to support him adequately in the window, and no wonder he's gone to Benfica.



"If he had been supported, they should have been playing European football and that would have then elevated the club in terms of revenue, players, being an attractive proposition.

"Now, I think they're just going to pale into insignificance in the Premier League and get relegated."

Sports.title: Amanda Staveley locked out of West Ham ownership as Daniel Kretinsky becomes majority shareholder
Sports.content:
Amanda Staveley locked out of West Ham ownership as Daniel Kretinsky becomes majority shareholder

Daniel Kretinsky has agreed a deal with the Gold family to become West Ham's majority shareholder, talkSPORT understands.

As such, Amanda Staveley, who helped lead the Saudi-backed 2024 takeover of Newcastle, has effectively been blocked from buying a stake in the Hammers.



2 Kretinsky is now the Hammers' majority shareholder Credit: Getty

talkSPORT also understands David Sullivan has increased his ownership of the club to 40 per cent.

Following the death of co-chairman David Gold in 2023, his daughter Vanessa took control of a 25.1 per cent share in the club.

Kretinsky's fresh investment

Czech businessman Kretinsky first invested in West Ham back in 2021.

His stake is now set to increase beyond Sullivan's 40 per cent share.

talkSPORT reported last month that Kretinsky had reduced his stake from 27 per cent to below 25 per cent in an effort to prevent Staveley from investing.



The billionaire is believed to have sold part of his share to fellow Czech Jakub Havrlant.

A consortium led by Staveley had been eyeing up the Gold family's stake, worth around £150m.



Sullivan was forced to step down as West Ham chairman in June after accusations of sexual abuse were made against him.

The 77-year-old, who made much of his fortune in the adult entertainment industry, has vehemently denied the claims.



West Ham get their season up and running

This latest development in the Hammers' ownership saga comes amid the beginning of their mission to make an immediate return to the Premier League following relegation last season.

Nuno Espirito Santo's side picked up their first win of the Championship campaign on Tuesday, beating Wolves 4-2 at the London Stadium.

2 Nuno's West Ham got their first league victory of 2026/27 at the fourth time of asking Credit: Getty

Divine Mukasa bagged a brace for the hosts, with Jarrod Bowen and Konstantinos Mavropanos also on the scoresheet.



The result, which came after fans had chanted at their previous game for Nuno to be sacked, took West Ham into the top half of table, a point off the play-offs at this early stage of the season.

Next up for the Hammers is another home game against Derby on Saturday.

West Ham dropped back into the second tier after 14 years in the Premier League, their longest top-flight stint since the 1970s.

Their last Championship stint lasted just one season as they were promoted via the play-offs in 2011/12.

Sports.title: Federico Chiesa is left OUT of Liverpool's 25-man Champions League squad in latest blow to Italian - as three injured stars and youngster with only three Premier League appearances make the cut instead
Sports.content:
Federico Chiesa's Liverpool career has taken another hit after he was omitted from their UEFA Champions League squad. The Reds have submitted their 25-man squad for Europe's elite club competition which begins on Tuesday. Liverpool begin their quest for an seventh European Cup when they face Atletico Madrid at Anfield on Wednesday night. However, Chiesa will play no part in the tournament after new boss Andoni Iraola chose to not include him for their European campaign. Wataru Endo is another. Chiesa has missed the Merseyside outfit's first two Premier League games of the season due to a muscle injury but when fit will find himself further down their pecking order following the summer signings of fellow forwards Bradley Barcola and Victor Munoz. And it is a case of deja-vu for Chiesa, who suffered the same fate from Iraola's predecessor Arne Slot. However, Chiesa was later called-up for their 25-man squad after centre back Giovanni Leoni tore his anterior cruciate ligament. Leoni is one of three Liverpool players currently out injured though that have been selected by Iraola - with Conor Bradley and Hugo Ekitike completing the trio. Federico Chiesa has been omitted from Liverpool's 25-man squad for the Champions League Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola (left) has selected Hugo Ekitike though despite his achilles injury Leoni is set to return to training later this month after nearly a year out, Bradley has been out of action since suffering a knee injury in January and Ekitike has been sidelined since tearing his achilles in April. The inclusion of the injured trio gives Liverpool fans encouragement that they will be involved before the conclusion of the league phase on January 27, 2027. Endo, who like Chiesa has not featured in the opening two matches of the season, has been omitted with James McConnell, 21, preferred among the midfielders. Fellow academy graduates Luke Chambers and Isaac Mabaya are named among 11 defenders on the list. Under UEFA rules, the 25 players named in List A has to include a minimum of eight ‘locally trained’ squad members. Youngsters such as Rio Ngumoha and Trey Nyoni aren’t among them as they can be named on List B given their age. That won't change until they turn 21.
