Sports.title: Rangers clinch double deadline-day deal by landing Kevin Kelsy and Badredine Bouanani
Sports.content:
Rangers clinch double deadline-day deal by landing Kevin Kelsy and Badredine Bouanani

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Rangers have completed a double deadline day swoop by signing Kevin Kelsy and Badredine Bouanani.

Kelsy was identified as a priority target when Youssef Chermiti sustained a serious knee injury against Hibernian last month.

The Venezuelan international forward has cost the Ibrox club £9.2million from MLS side Portland Timbers and has signed a four-year deal with an option of a fifth.

The 22-year-old gives manager Derek McInnes another option up front to compete with Lawrence Shankland, Ryan Naderi and Bojan Miovski.

The fee is the second highest in Rangers’ history, second only to the £12m spent on Tore Andre Flo in 2000.

Kelsy came through the ranks of Mineros de Guayana in his home country then moved to Uruguayan outfit Boston River for a short spell before joining Shakhtar Donetsk in January, 2023.

Rangers unveiled the £9million signing of striker Kevin Kelsy from Portland Timbers

The Ibrox club also secured the loan addition of Algerian Badredine Bouanani from Stuttgart

He then joined Portland Timbers in January 2025 after a loan spell at FC Cincinnati.

‘I’ve heard a lot about the club,’ he said. ‘Even when I was younger, I saw the team in Europe. I know what the club means to the fans.

‘I would love to bring some joy to the fans and the club, and score goals to bring amazing moments to the team.

‘I know we have to win all the games and play well, and I’ll be ready for this with my teammates. I’m ready for this new chapter in my life.’

Boss Derek McInnes said: ‘We’re really pleased to welcome Kevin to the club. He’s an exciting player with a lot of attributes, and what really stood out in our conversations is how hungry he is to make an impact.

‘He’ll bring real quality to an area of the pitch we have been keen to strengthen, and his arrival gives us another exciting option going forward.

‘Kevin has a great attitude and a real desire to improve, and we’re looking forward to seeing what he can bring at Rangers.’

Bouanani, 21, has arrived on a year’s loan from Stuttgart, where he operated on the right wing.

The Algerian moved to Germany from Nice in 2025 having played and scored against Rangers for the French club in a European match.

The pair’s arrivals mean Rangers have signed 14 players in this window — either permanently or on loan.

Thelo Aasgaard has gone in the other direction after moving on loan to Anderlecht, while Nico Raskin is staying at the club after Rangers turned down a second bid from Turkish side Besiktas.

Sports.title: Naomi Osaka calls on US Open influencers to 'read up on tennis etiquette' after umpire was forced to tell off spectators during her first match
Sports.content:
Naomi Osaka called upon influencers travelling to the US Open to 'read up' on the sport's rules for spectators after her first-round match was disrupted by a rowdy group in one of Arthur Ashe Stadium's luxury suites.

The four-time Grand Slam champion had been preparing to serve when the chair umpire told off the guests for appearing to stage an impromptu photoshoot, complete with portable lights.

'Guys, please, in the suite behind me, please thank you guys, please take your seat,' the chair umpire announced to the stadium, as the broadcast camera panned to a group milling freely within their prime seats, taking pictures and talking.

While Osaka was only half-focused on the specifics of the incident while immersed in defeating her opponent Anastasia Zakharova, discussing what happened on the tournament's showcourt two days later, she suggested that more could be done to ensure that players were not disturbed during matchplay.

'I think obviously, if you come to a sporting event, you have to respect the sport,' she said after her defeat of Katerina Siniakova, which took place on the same court. 'And I feel like it's common courtesy to read up on the sport, especially the etiquette.

'I feel like it could be a good thing for people to make the sport of tennis popular to their specific audience, but I think it has to be managed a lot better, especially in the situation like first-round match.

Naomi Osaka called for fans new to tennis to learn the sport's etiquette after her match was disrupted by influencers

'Overall I think there is huge positives,' she added, on the topic of influencers more generally. 'You want people to continue to grow the sport. I just think it has to be in a way that everyone knows the rules and the etiquette.'

Etiquette largely dictates that fans should save conversation and movement for changeovers or set breaks, when the players are at the chairs. But in 2024, the US Open switched to a policy of 'free fan movement', which allows spectators to move during points regardless of on-court action.

Of the incident itself, Osaka said that she had been more bothered by the noise inside the stadium during both her matches - a constant chatter which complements the endless movement - than the flash lights themselves.

'I was going to say today the umpire, she told everyone to be quiet more than I've ever heard an umpire tell a crowd to be quiet,' she continued.

'I do think in my first match, I wasn't really paying attention. I tell people I normally just focus on the match and the court, but there was a moment where there was, like, people shouting, and you could hear it quite clearly. I think it bothered my opponent, too.

'Maybe that's what you were talking about, but I've heard some people say, like, the lights or whatever. I don't really see the lights, because obviously, when you are serving, you're looking at the sun or you're looking at the night lights. It was more the noise.'

Daily Mail Sport contacted the tournament for comment on after Osaka's press conference, with US Open head of communications Brendan McIntyre sharing the following statement: 'The USTA is always striving to grow tennis in this country and bring new audiences into the sport. The US Open is our greatest opportunity to do so, and we welcome newcomers to our event.

'We want all of our fans and guests to have an incredible time when they attend, but we also need to ensure they do not interfere with the action and competition on the court. We are continually looking for ways to ensure fans in the stands know what is permitted and what is prohibited.

'As a result, we have increased signage on the grounds and in stadium, and messaged ticket and suite holders to remind everyone to refrain from any activity that could disrupt the game, including noise levels, flash photography and ring lights. The chair umpire also has the ability to address the crowd if and when necessary.'

READ MORE - How influencers are killing the US Open and turning it into a 'zoo': Angry top stars hit out at 'disrespectful' and noisy content creators disrupting matches for pictures

Sports.title: How influencers are killing the US Open and turning it into a 'zoo': Angry top stars hit out at 'disrespectful' and noisy content creators disrupting matches for pictures
Sports.content:
Naomi Osaka was not having the easiest time on court. Having battled through a tie-break to edge the first set, she was serving at 4-4 in the second. Then, her concentration snapped.

Up in the luxury suites, a group of influencers were posing for photographs using a bright, portable light. As they milled about the box, unaware of the tension below, their distraction was enough to prompt a warning from the chair umpire. But it took a few moments for the message to filter through. After all, their focus was on getting the perfect shot.

Welcome to the 2026 US Open. Long the envy of the Grand Slams for the late-night energy and glamour that only New York can provide, this year's tournament has been subject to complaints about being overrun with influencers who see the final major of the year as little more than a creative backdrop on social media.

'People are down there trying to perform, and it's their career and their job. It seems like a bit disrespectful,' US No 1 Jessica Pegula said when asked about the incident in Osaka's match after her own bow on Arthur Ashe, the tournament's biggest court. 'I think it's gotten a little too much, it feels, this year.'

There's no mystery behind why the US Open has become such a popular destination to tick off for the well-travelled influencer.

'The US Open has evolved from a tennis tournament into one of the most powerful cultural points on the New York calendar,' notes Reece Milner, Senior Strategy Manager at The Goat Agency, a creator and influencer marketing shop. 'It now sits at the intersection of sport, fashion, luxury, hospitality, celebrity, lifestyle and content culture.'

The 'rituals' that appear so frequently on social media feeds that you might be able to play US Open bingo, like enjoying a night match, a Honey Deuce cocktail or $100 COQODAQ chicken nugget-and-caviar box, Milner adds, have only served to crystallise its status.

A group of influencers caught flack for using a portable light to take pictures during Naomi Osaka's match

The US Open has seen a huge rise in popularity in recent years and brands hosting influencers at the tournament in a bid to borrow its cultural clout has risen too

This is no one-way street either, with the US Open well aware of its cultural power outside of tennis as well as within. The tournament has embraced the influencer, this year going as far as to credential 100 content creators, with US Open head of communications Brendan McIntyre noting that in years to come, the number is only going to 'go upwards'.

But those influencers aren't necessarily the problem. Tennis media has evolved to take in TikTok, Instagram, and Substack experts, all invested in growing interest in the game itself. More worthy of skepticism are those who might be spending one night at the Open, making it a race against time to get the perfect picture, action on court be damned.

The US Open has never been Wimbledon, and that's a good thing. The noise of an Arthur Ashe night session makes for pleasing whiplash after the prim-and-proper hush of Centre Court as the tour bounces between the two majors.

But as greater numbers of guests flood into the Billie Jean King National Tennis Center with limited interest in the tennis and more on their feed, the noise levels of ambient chatter, rather than engagement in the match, have caused problems for players.

'On Ashe, you hear everything,' Pegula added. 'Even when there's dead noise, there's still a buzz or a chatter or people talking and eating and laughing and all these different kind of emotions. You really have to do a good job of locking yourself in a bubble when you're out there.'

Of fans on the outdoor courts, French player Adrian Mannarino was more forthright: 'They come in any which way, they move around, they talk. It's the tournament that tolerates this, and I don't know if it's the best idea for the game in general. There's noise coming from everywhere. It's become a bit of a zoo.'

Watching Aryna Sabalenka and Carlos Alcaraz on Arthur Ashe on Wednesday, the noise of the crowd never dipped below 'pub garden'. Since the tournament ushered in 'free fan movement' in 2024 which allows fans to come and go without waiting for changeovers or set breaks, the policy has been followed to the letter, with the lower bowl constantly in motion.

Influencers have added to the heat around the US Open and their enviable photographs will have translated, in part, to ticket sales

Inside Arthur Ashe Stadium is a constant hum of noise as fans move in their seats during points

That's where most of the chatter comes from too, with the seats in the gods crammed with fans locked in on the action, and quieter during play.

As Alcaraz took the first game after losing his opening set to Jaime Faria, the noise rises to a roar, with the same staticky thickness of a sound machine playing a recording of the ocean at full volume. At 0-15, clearly distracted, the Portuguese player serves a double fault. The chair umpire gives a warning when a fan shouts down from the stands as he's preparing to serve again, but does little to dim the constant conversation.

Nor have those in the suites learned their lesson. Despite the US Open displaying messages around the site telling fans to refrain from using flash or lights to take pictures, Daily Mail Sport spotted flashes going off during Sabalenka's thrashing of Polina Iatcenko.

A statement shared after the Osaka incident placed the responsibility for wrangling misbehaving influencers on the chair umpires, who 'have the ability to address the crowd' when 'infrequent' disruptions occur. On Thursday, an extended second statement responding to Osaka's comments added that the tournament has 'increased signage on the grounds and in stadium, and messaged ticket and suite holders to remind everyone to refrain from any activity that could disrupt the game, including noise levels, flash photography and ring lights.'

Influencers have added to the heat around the US Open and their enviable photographs will have translated, in part, to ticket sales. But if the goal is to get more fans into the sport, week-in, week-out, they need great tennis played in a great tennis atmosphere - and inside on the tournament's biggest courts, that can no longer be guaranteed.

Sports.title: FIFA accuse UEFA of a 'smear campaign' against Gianni Infantino and Co after European body threatened legal action as war over failed World Cup sell-off plans escalates
Sports.content:
FIFA accuse UEFA of a 'smear campaign' against Gianni Infantino and Co after European body threatened legal action as war over failed World Cup sell-off plans escalates

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

FIFA says legal applications made by UEFA to access documents related to FIFA's controversial private investor plan are part of a 'smear campaign' against the global governing body.

UEFA is applying through the American courts for discovery of evidence and documentation linked to FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE), a private company which it was envisaged would run the World Cup and other FIFA competitions.

FIFA confirmed last month the plan had been to sell a 20 per cent stake in that company to private investors. The plan was withdrawn by FIFA president Gianni Infantino on August 1 amid opposition from UEFA, the Asian Football Confederation (AFC) and CONCACAF, the confederation for countries in North and Central America plus the Caribbean.

That withdrawal has not stopped UEFA pursuing Infantino and other FIFA officials, with UEFA saying documents obtained were intended for use in preparing potential criminal proceedings in Switzerland, in filings seen by the Press Association on August 27.

The following day, FIFA sought approval to oppose UEFA's request in the Southern District of Florida, a motion which was granted by the court on the next business day, August 31. FIFA has until September 28 to submit a full opposition to that court.

A similar motion to oppose was also filed in the Southern District of New York on Tuesday. Documents from FIFA's legal team seen by the Press Association describe UEFA's applications as being 'little more than press releases in further support of UEFA's smear campaign against FIFA and its leadership'.

UEFA president Aleksander Ceferin (left) and FIFA counterpart Gianni Infantino are at loggerheads over the latter's failed proposals for World Cup private investor plans

FIFA's filing asks the New York court to defer consideration on UEFA's discovery application until the Florida court has ruled on it, or requests that the court permit FIFA permission to oppose UEFA's application no later than September 30.

The filing said UEFA's motivation in its opposition to FFE and Infantino was 'to prevent smaller countries from having the financial strength to compete with the European elite'.

It added: 'If soccer is strengthened in the developing world, global competition increases, which ultimately reduces UEFA's market power and provides more competition for its flagship tournaments.

'By raising funds to allow some of FIFA's smaller member associations to better develop soccer, FFE would lead to more players from those nations choosing to represent their countries of origin and playing in their home leagues rather than playing abroad.

'All of this would erode UEFA's dominance over other regions of the world.'

UEFA's filing accused Infantino of 'criminal mismanagement' in relation to FFE, and said the proposed sale of a stake for £3.1billion ($4.2bn) in the company was 'a fraudulently off-market price promoted by Infantino for his own benefit'.

In a separate statement published last week, UEFA called for an independent external review of the origins of the FFE and said that if Infantino chose to stand for re-election at next year's FIFA Congress, UEFA would 'join forces with its partner confederations to ensure that member associations are offered a credible alternative - one committed to integrity, accountability, development and genuine institutional change'.

Sports.title: Aston Villa handed major boost as new £60m star Johan Manzambi returns to training - but he may not be risked for Hull clash
Sports.content:
Aston Villa handed major boost as new £60m star Johan Manzambi returns to training - but he may not be risked for Hull clash

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Johan Manzambi trained with his Aston Villa team-mates on Thursday fuelling hopes that his debut could arrive sooner than expected.

The club-record signing from Freiburg had a knee injury when he joined Villa in July in a deal worth up to £60million, and he has yet to play as he continues his recovery.

Yet Daily Mail Sport understands Manzambi took part in Thursday's session, though it is unclear at this stage whether he would be considered for Saturday's trip to Hull, where Villa will hope to claim their first points of the season after consecutive defeats to Brighton and Arsenal.

After the 1-0 home defeat by Arsenal on August 31, Emery was cautious about Manzambi, though he hoped the 20-year-old would be able to join in this week.

He said: 'We must be careful. He had an injury and we want his comeback to be clear and strong, with no risk.

'Progressively, he is working individually and is starting collectively with the group this week.'

Johan Manzambi trained with his Aston Villa team-mates on Thursday as he stepped up his recovery

After losing key members of the team who lifted the Europa League and qualified for the Champions League last term, Villa have tried to rebuild by making 11 signings. Emery has also brought forward Brian Madjo and midfielder George Hemmings into the first-team group.

Morgan Rogers moved to Chelsea this summer for a record £117m, with Emi Martinez also making the switch to Stamford Bridge. Youri Tielemans, Lucas Digne, Ollie Watkins and Ezri Konsa also departed in a summer of huge change at Villa Park.

Sports.title: Roy Keane goes viral after leaving Gary Neville and Co in stitches with hilarious comparison between football stat and 'speaking to girls in a nightclub'
Sports.content:
Roy Keane goes viral after leaving Gary Neville and Co in stitches with hilarious comparison between football stat and 'speaking to girls in a nightclub'

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Roy Keane left his Stick to Football colleagues in fits of laughter following his thoughts about the statistic 'Expected Goals' (xG).

Speaking on the latest episode of the show, brought to you by Disney+, the former Manchester United captain expressed why he believes that particular stat - which measures the probability that a given shot will result in a goal - is irrelevant.

Sitting alongside Gary Neville, Jamie Carragher, Jill Scott and Ian Wright, Keane started his point animatedly with: 'Do you know what that stat is?

'Years ago, when you'd go to a nightclub back in the day, and you'd chat to a girl all night, but you go home by yourself. What's your xG?'

Keane's quip left Neville, Carragher, Scott and Wright in stitches. Neville then replied self-depreciatingly: 'Roy, I kept clean sheets!'

A smirking Roy said: 'I'm sure you did, yeah!'

xG explained the Roy Keane way! 🤣 pic.twitter.com/qJOS705noc — The Overlap (@WeAreTheOverlap) September 3, 2026

Roy Keane left his Stick to Football colleagues laughing with his views on Expected Goals (xG)

Gary Neville (left) and Jamie Carragher were in hysterics after Keane compared it to nightclubs

During the show, the quintet discussed the closing of the summer transfer window - following Tuesday's 11pm deadline.

Among the clubs discussed was Liverpool - with Carragher believing Reds boss Andoni Iraola needs to have an awkward conversation with his vice-captain Dominik Szoboszlai and move him to right back permanently.

Szoboszlai, 25, was rewarded with a new £350,000-a-week contract this summer after being named Liverpool’s Player of the Season for his impressive performances in midfield last campaign - one of the few positives in what was otherwise a disappointing season for the Reds under Arne Slot.

Despite establishing himself as a mainstay in midfield, the Hungarian has also been called upon to deputise at right-back, doing so sporadically last season and again during the second half of Liverpool’s 2-2 draw with Nottingham Forest on Saturday.

Carragher believes Szoboszlai may be tasked with the right-back role permanently after Liverpool's disjointed start under Iraola, who has drawn both his Premier League matches so far.

With Conor Bradley still injured and Jeremie Frimpong struggling for form, right-back has become a problem position for Liverpool since Trent Alexander-Arnold's exit to Real Madrid last summer.

Fearing it was a 'massive mistake' not to bolster Liverpool's ranks at full back in the transfer window, Carragher is confident Szoboszlai could provide a solution for Iraola.

Carragher believes Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola (right) needs to have an awkward conversation with his vice-captain Dominik Szoboszlai (left) and move him to right-back

'The big thing he (Iraola) has got, and it happened last season and at the weekend, Szoboszlai went back to right-back. I've never believed Szoboszlai is a central midfield player,' Carragher said.

'Now, he's signed a new contract and I can only imagine in those talks, they were desperate for him to stay, he's almost said "I want to play midfield". He's moved around a bit and he started the season in central midfield. I don't see him as that.

'For me, in midfield he's a Jordan Henderson. Runner, energy, with more of a goal threat. But Liverpool don't play that way and he's not really a No 10. His best role could actually be at right-back. He'd get plenty of the ball, he can run and almost play that Trent role from there.

'But there's no way he's going to want to play there because he's just signed a new contract for £350,000 a week. You've just done this big thing, he's the vice-captain, I just think that's a conversation Iraola is going to have to have going forward, because the midfield is not right and he's part of that midfield not being right.'

Sports.title: David Sullivan to INCREASE stake in West Ham despite sexual misconduct allegations - with Royal Mail chief to become largest shareholder in huge blow to Amanda Staveley
Sports.content:
David Sullivan to INCREASE stake in West Ham despite sexual misconduct allegations - with Royal Mail chief to become largest shareholder in huge blow to Amanda Staveley

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Daniel Kretinsky is set to become the largest shareholder at West Ham United – with David Sullivan also increasing his stake in the club.

In a move that would deliver a major blow to Amanda Staveley, who had reached an initial agreement to buy the Gold family’s 25.1 per cent stake in the Championship outfit, Czech billionaire Kretinsky is thought to have exercised pre-emption rights.

It means Kretinsky, along with the other existing shareholders, will instead split the Golds' holding, leaving former Newcastle United director Staveley in the cold.

Terms of the deal are yet to be disclosed however, it is understood that, as a result, Royal Mail owner Kretinsky will up his stake from 27 to 46 per cent, with Sullivan – who stood down as joint-chairman in June in the wake of serious allegations that he abused his power by preying on women for sex – increasing his holding from 38.8 per cent to 40 per cent. American investor Tripp Smith would expand his share from 8 to 11 per cent, with the remaining shareholders rising from 1.1 to 3 per cent.

Former West Ham joint-chairman David Sullivan is set to increase his stake in the club

Sullivan, 77, ‘categorically’ denies the claims against him. He is banned from having one-to-one contact or direct access to the Hammers women’s and youth teams following a historical complaint to the FA. The Independent Football Regulator said it would seek ‘urgent information’ regarding the allegations from Sullivan, and also contacted Essex Police.

West Ham have been contacted for comment. Staveley had offered £150m for the Gold stake, which some viewed as the first step towards a full takeover.

Sports.title: Gabriel Martinelli savagely SNUBS Mikel Arteta following 'uncomfortable' end to Arsenal career
Sports.content:
Gabriel Martinelli savagely SNUBS Mikel Arteta following 'uncomfortable' end to Arsenal career

Gabriel Martinelli has completed a £60m move to Al-Hilal after leaving Arsenal, and his farewell message made no mention of manager Mikel Arteta

View 2 Images Gabriel Martinelli spent seven years at Arsenal before his departure (Image: Marc Atkins/Getty Images)

Gabriel Martinelli has sent a farewell message to Arsenal following his move to Saudi Arabia, but the Brazilian did not mention Mikel Arteta in his post. The 25-year-old completed a £60million switch to Al Hilal, which was confirmed on Thursday evening.

‌



Martinelli was granted a move away from Arsenal after the reigning Premier League champions signed Christos Tzolis from Club Brugge, who will compete with Ebere Eze for the left wing spot in the starting line-up.

‌



The Brazilian was linked with a move to Turkey, as well as Saudi Arabia, before going in to complete a switch to the Saudi Pro League.

‌



Martinelli made the trip to the Middle East earlier this week to undergo a medical to become an Al Hilal player and was officially unveiled by the club on Thursday.

Arsenal confirm £60m Gabriel Martinelli transfer as star exits in record deal READ MORE :

Arsenal medical underway with third Gunners signing already lined up for 2027 READ MORE :

Arsenal went on to send a message of appreciation to Martinelli following the confirmation of his departure.

The club posted: "Forever a Gunner. The club can confirm that Gabriel Martinelli has joined Al-Hilal on a permanent deal. Thank you for everything and best of luck, Gabi."

‌



Martinelli also took to social media to share a heartfelt message of his own to the club, though notably, without even mentioning Arteta after suggestions that their relationship had broken down.

He posted: "I can only thank the staff and my teammates. Thank you to the chefs, kit staff, doctors, doormen, security staff, media team, cleaning staff, physios, and every single teammate who has been part of my story from 2019 until today. Thank you to everyone who helped me grow during this journey.

"And to the fans, thank you for everything. Since my first day, you made me feel at home. Every time I stepped on the pitch, despite everything, I tried to give everything I had for this shirt. To Arsenal, thank you for believing in me and giving me the chance to show myself to the world.

‌



View 2 Images Gabriel Martinelli posted a farewell message to Arsenal supporters (Image: Catherine Ivill - AMA/Getty Images)

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

"Most of all, I want to thank my family and my wife, who have been by my side throughout this entire journey, giving me all the emotional support I needed to overcome the challenges that only we truly know. It has been a long journey, too much history and now it has come to an end.

‌



"I’m writing this with tears in my eyes, so hard to put 7 years into words. From 35 to 11. Once a Gunner, Always a Gunner. Goodbye, and thank you again."

This follows Ian Wright criticising the club's treatment of Martinelli behind closed doors in the build-up to his exit, citing how "uncomfortable" the situation from his former club made him feel.

Speaking with Sky Sports after Arsenal's opening night win against Coventry City, Wright explained: "With respect to Martinelli and the way he’s being treated at the moment, it really makes me uncomfortable.

‌



"He always gives 100%, we’re not saying he’s the greatest, but he’s come up with some big moments for Arsenal in big games, and the way he’s being treated at the end here – I know they might want him out and there’s a lot of guys saying it’s time for him to move on, but there’s ways of doing that should suit him as well."

Asked what he meant by the treatment, Wright added: "Not being in the squad tonight, not being spoken to, doesn’t know what’s going on."

‌



He continued: "Yes I do know this, I know this. Not being involved in the Community Shield squad, not being involved tonight, he doesn’t know what’s happening, he’s got a year left.

"If you bring Vini in, that kind of level, Martinelli can say to himself, ‘Well okay they’ve brought him in and Tzolis, I might be third.' But if you’re bringing in Tzolis and Madueke’s there, you’re thinking to yourself, ‘I’ve got something to offer here.'

"So for him to be nowhere near it, just makes me feel a bit sad for him. I think he’s done enough in this squad to be treated with a bit more respect than he’s been treated at the moment."

Sports.title: Richarlison AXED from Tottenham's Premier League squad after botched Everton move
Sports.content:
Richarlison AXED from Tottenham's Premier League squad after botched Everton move

Richarlison is set to be frozen out at Tottenham unless he is able to agree a transfer overseas after a potential return to the striker's former club Everton collapsed

View 2 Images Richarlison has omitted from Tottenham's Premier League squad (Image: Marc Atkins, Getty Images)

Richarlison has not been included in Tottenham's squad for the Premier League this season, with the striker now free to explore a move abroad.

‌



Spurs have spent heavily this summer to overhaul their squad after two disastrous Premier League campaigns, with the likes of Sandro Tonali, Mateus Fernandes and Savio all signing for significant transfer fees. Omar Marmoush has also arrived in attack on loan with an obligation to make the move permanent next summer, nudging Richarlison further down the pecking order.

‌



It seemed as though a return to the Brazilian's former club, Everton, was in the offing in the final knockings of the transfer window with Tottenham in turn lining up a move for Iliman Ndiaye.

‌



But both deals collapsed with Ndiaye subsequently joining Manchester City - and Richarlison now faces being left out in the cold if he remains in north London.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

It's been confirmed that the 29-year-old has been omitted from Spurs squad, meaning he is unable to feature in Premier League games for the first half of the season.

‌



One option for the former Watford striker is a move overseas with several international transfer windows still open. Turkey is one such option and there has been interest in Richarlison's services from Trabzonspor, who have already seen a bid for his services rebuffed by Tottenham. Saudi Pro League clubs can also still sign players and could offer Richarlison a career lifeline.

The player, who was left out of the Tottenham squad which lost 2-0 against Newcastle on Saturday, has just one year remaining on his current contract.

A return to Everton, where he enjoyed a successful four year spell before moving to Spurs, looked to tick all the boxes in the final hours of the transfer window. However, Richarlison took to social media to explain why a move would not go through.

‌



View 2 Images Richarlison was a huge hit at Everton before joining Spurs but a potential return to Merseyside collapsed (Image: Getty Images )

“After everything I’ve been through in the last few years, I’ve decided that never again will anyone decide my future for me,” he wrote. “I went through a lot of bad things, and almost all of them happened because decisions were made by other people. Pressure, threats, retaliation — none of that scares me. I’ve been through far worse, believe me.

“I always made it clear, on every occasion, that if I were to leave for another place, it would also have to be good for the club. If it wasn’t, I would never accept it… just as I didn’t when everything here was falling apart and they needed me. I stayed and gave my life to it.

Article continues below

“So, I hope they treat my situation with the same respect that I have always had for Spurs and for everyone who has worked with me during this period. Just don’t try to decide for me.”

Sports.title: Arsenal to avoid same looming transfer concern as Liverpool and Man Utd
Sports.content:
Arsenal to avoid same looming transfer concern as Liverpool and Man Utd

Arsenal endured a frustrating summer transfer window after failing to land any of their marquee attacking targets but there is some good news for Mikel Arteta

View 3 Images Mikel Arteta and Arsenal are out to win the Premier League title again (Image: (Visionhaus/Getty Images))

Arsenal entered the summer transfer window with grand ambitions after once again establishing themselves as the champions of England.

‌



The main goal for Mikel Arteta and Co, after ending a 22-year wait for another Premier League title, was to level up the squad that also came within a whisker of winning the Champions League for the first time in the club's history. Particularly in attack, where it was accepted that upgrades were needed if they were to meet Arteta's demands in creating 'a dynasty'.

‌



Unfortunately, Arsenal were unable to acquire the elite attacker they craved despite their dogged pursuit of genuine game-changer targets in the form of Morgan Rogers and Vinicius Junior.

‌



The Gunners can at least take solace from the fact that their squad remains seriously strong and, on paper, perfectly capable of retaining their domestic crown. And although this transfer window may not have gone totally to plan, they could even hold an advantage over their title rivals when it comes to future windows.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

With Gabriel Martinelli now on the cusp of finalising his £60million transfer to Al-Hilal, Arsenal will have no players out of contract next summer. That means they are free to plan ahead without the distraction of trying to tie down key figures to longer terms while allocating their available resources into planned new additions.

‌



Arsenal's situation is likely to be the envy of both Liverpool and Manchester United, who find themselves with plenty of big contract decisions to make over the next few months.

View 3 Images Virgil van Dijk is among a handful of senior Liverpool players who could be free agents next summer (Image: Michael Driver/MI News/NurPhoto via Getty Images)

Liverpool have five first-team players whose deals are up next summer, including that of club captain, Virgil van Dijk. The Dutchman is joined by Alisson, Joe Gomez, Konstantinos Tsimkas and Wataru Endo, while the Reds will also have to decide whether or not to trigger the option to buy Ronald Araujo following his loan move from Barcelona.

‌



Some decisions may be more clear-cut than others but with key figures such as Van Dijk and Alisson now in the twilight years of their career, there is definitely plenty for the Anfield hierarchy to ponder.

At Old Trafford, there are also some big-hitters who could potentially leave for nothing in 12 months time. The standout name is Bruno Fernandes, thought it has been suggested that United have already reopened contract negotiations with their captain.

View 3 Images Manchester United will need to tie their captain and talisman Bruno Fernandes down to a longer deal

‌



Seven other players are due to be free agents next summer including first team regulars Harry Maguire, Luke Shaw and Lisandro Martinez. Again, it feels like there is plenty for United to consider given the ages of their important defenders.

Harry Amass, Jack Fletcher and Tyler Fletcher are also now inside the final year of their contracts, as is United's veteran goalkeeper, Tom Heaton.

Sports.title: Arsenal confirm £60m Gabriel Martinelli transfer as star exits in record deal
Sports.content:
Arsenal confirm £60m Gabriel Martinelli transfer as star exits in record deal

Arsenal attacker Gabriel Martinelli has finally completed a huge £60million transfer to the Saudi Pro League after accepting an offer to join Al-Hilal

View 2 Images Gabriel Martinelli has joined Al Hilal (Image: Getty Images)

Gabriel Martinelli has been confirmed as an Al-Hilal player following the conclusion of his £60million transfer from Arsenal.

‌



The Brazilian winger, 25, departs the Emirates for a club-record transfer fee following the Premier League champions' decision to refresh their attack in the transfer window. The £60m fee far eclipses the previous record for an Arsenal sale, which was set by Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain's £35m switch to Liverpool back in 2017.

‌



Martinelli's future has been in doubt for months with speculation linking Arsenal with some supremely talented and expensive left wing options such as Morgan Rogers and Vinicius Junior.

‌



But with the Gunners failing to acquire either player, or an alternative in the final days of the transfer window, Christos Tzolis is the only new attacker they have added to their ranks.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Martinelli turned down a move to Galatasaray last month and was left out of the team for both of Arsenal's Premier League games so far this term.

‌



He departs Arsenal after making 53 appearances in all competitions last season, scoring 11 goals.

The Gunners paid tribute to Martinelli's contributions in a statement confirming the transfer, which read: "Gabriel Martinelli has joined Saudi Pro League side Al-Hilal on a permanent transfer.

"Gabi joined us from Brazilian club Ituano in July 2019 and went on to make 278 appearances for the club in all competitions, scoring 62 goals.

‌



View 2 Images Martinelli found himself surplus to requirements this season (Image: Nick Potts/PA Wire)

"During his seven years with us, the 25-year-old played an integral role in helping us win the Premier League last season, the FA Cup in 2020 and the FA Community Shield in 2023.

"In that time, Gabi also established himself as a Brazil international, earning 27 caps and representing his country at the 2020 Summer Olympics in Tokyo, where he won a gold medal, as well as the 2024 Copa America and the 2022 and 2026 FIFA World Cups.

Article continues below

"Everyone at Arsenal would like to thank Gabi for his contribution to the club and wish him and his family well for the future."

Sports.title: Arsenal medical underway with third Gunners signing already lined up for 2027
Sports.content:
Arsenal medical underway with third Gunners signing already lined up for 2027

Arsenal are sorting a medical for FC Kolkheti-1913 Poti teenager Andria Bartishvili, with the 17-year-old set to sign a five-year contract and officially join the Premier League champions in 2027

View Image Mikel Arteta could add another youngster to his Arsenal squad next summer (Image: Nick Potts/PA Wire)

Arsenal are closing in on the signing of FC Kolkheti-1913 Poti star Andria Bartishvili, with the playmaker having a medical today. The Gunners have spent the summer preparing their squad for another Premier League title challenge, but have also had an eye on the future with deals to sign stars for the future.

‌



As has been reported by football.london, Arsenal have agreed a €4.5million (£3.9million) deal to sign the 17-year-old playmaker, although he will not move to the Emirates Stadium this summer.

‌



Instead, it’s understood that Bartishvili will officially become an Arsenal player in 12 months time, which will also coincide with the arrivals of Ecuadorian twins Holger and Edwin Quintero from Independiente.

‌



This will also be when Bartishvili turns 18, where he will be expected to sign a five-year contract to move to Arsenal.

Arsenal deal for Bruno Guimaraes rated one out of 10 in brutal transfer ranking READ MORE :

It is understood that Bartishvili was present at the Sobha Realty Training Centre on Thursday to undergo a medical and finalise the remaining details surrounding his switch to the Gunners.

The youngster is set to become the fourth young talent snapped up by Arsenal ahead of a prospective future arrival, following Victor Ozhianvuna's move from Shamrock Rovers in January.

‌



Georgian football expert Saba Sapanadze spoke to football.london regarding Arsenal's quest to sign Bartishvili, and why the fee agreed for the playmaker represents exceptional value for the Premier League champions.

“I think Arsenal were very lucky to get Andria for €4.5million,” Sapanadze said. “That only happened because he’s Georgian, otherwise I genuinely believe his price would have been around €15million-€20million.

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



“Why? Because he is considered one of the biggest talents in the country, alongside [Khvicha] Kvaratskhelia’s brother, Tornike.”

Sapanadze runs Geo Team, a Georgian football platform that delivers updates on players from the country, and proceeded to outline why he anticipates Bartishvili will join the first team in training upon his arrival next year, after which a loan could be an option.

“Let’s be realistic. Arsenal have an incredible squad right now, so it would be unrealistic for me to tell you that he’ll walk straight into the first team,” he said.

‌



“However, from what I understand, he’ll have a first-team contract and will train with the senior squad.

“Perhaps, initially, a loan to the Championship for regular playing time could be a smart move and help him adapt to British football.”

‌



Arsenal experienced a relatively quiet summer transfer window following their Premier League title success earlier this year, with four new additions confirmed by the club.

Bruno Guimaraes, Ezri Konsa, Christos Tzolis and Illan Meslier have all been brought in by Arsenal this summer, as Mikel Arteta and Co. look to retain their crown.

Liverpool registered an interest in the Crystal Palace winger during the summer transfer window

Ismaila Sarr declared his love for Manchester United before Liverpool held an interest in signing him. The Crystal Palace winger was the subject of transfer speculation as Anfield chiefs searched for another wide forward in the summer transfer window.

Sports.title: Moses Itauma has stunning claim debunked after Filip Hrgovic loss
Sports.content:
Moses Itauma has stunning claim debunked after Filip Hrgovic loss

Fabio Wardley has had his say on gym-mate Moses Itauma's claim that he has never trained 12 rounds after the Brit gassed out against Filip Hrgovic

View Image Moses Itauma with Ben Davison after his defeat to Filip Hrgovic (Image: Getty Images)

Fabio Wardley has debunked Moses Itauma's remarkable claim, ahead of his loss to Filip Hrgovic, that he has never trained 12 rounds.

‌



The Chatham southpaw was beaten for the first time in his professional career on Saturday night, despite dominating the majority of the contest. Itauma was cruising until he gassed out and was eventually stopped by the Croatian heavyweight brawler in the ninth round.

‌



Many within the world of boxing were quick to slam Itauma's trainer, Ben Davison, for failing to prepare the Brit for a 12-round war. The 21-year-old's conditioning came into question after he spent all of his energy in the opening rounds trying to knock his foe out. Several were also quick to point the finger at Itauma's pre-fight claim, in which he hinted that he had yet to spar for 12 rounds.

‌



But team-mate Wardley - who is also trained by Davison - has shut down those remarks. During an interview with talkSPORT, he said: "I know Moses did do twelve rounds multiple times. He did it in the build-up to the fight, not before when that interview was done.

FOLLOW OUR FIGHTING FB PAGE! Latest boxing and MMA news, analysis and much more via our dedicated Facebook page

Tyson Fury provides Anthony Joshua fight update with talks on brink of collapse READ MORE :

Moses Itauma told exactly what went wrong during Filip Hrgovic loss READ MORE :

"There's a reason for that because you build up towards something, so he may have done eight rounders, tens, then finished on twelves. We are big heavy guys, we don't do 12 rounds sparring all the time, we wouldn't make it to the fight. You have to be savvy about how you prepare for a fight, camps are long, you have to balance it well enough."

‌



In the days that have followed, Davison has been faced with calls to be sacked by Itauma, but Wardley has been quick to defend his trainer. He told reporters, including Mirror Fighting, on Wednesday morning: I've been overwhelmed, I think, by the amount of criticism he's received and just almost in shock of just like, I don't know another trainer in British boxing that gets so much stick after a loss.

Tyson Fury recruits Mike Tyson to call out Anthony Joshua and get deal over the line READ MORE :

"It makes, I find it bemusing, like it's delusional to me. So yeah, if anything, that's added a bit of fuel to me to be like, all right, fine, no worries. I'll show you what us, the team, Ben Davison, what we can all do. I'll prove it to you. I'll take that on my shoulders. I'll wear that, no problem.

He added: "He's taught me so much about boxing in terms of actually how to read it. Like if you look at my history and how I came into it, I came into it very fresh. I came into it literally just throwing hands, just thinking, oh, boxing is you punch that person or you punch him more than he punches you. But there's so many different details and nuances that I've learned and picked up over the years. And if you look at my fights, I have applied them.

Article continues below

"But, if you go back, if you look at me pre-Ben and look at me post-Ben, you can see the stark differences. But also that plus, using a football term, I guess, is the man management. Is knowing the guy in front of you and knowing his strengths and weaknesses.

"For me, I'm not the best boxer in the world. I'm not an Alexander Usyk. I'm not going to out point, out box, out do these guys. But I do have athletic power and a bunch of other advantages that we know how to double down on and use. And that's where good man management and a good team comes into play."

Sports.title: Alexander Isak and £35m goal machine will have Man Utd excited after last-minute deal
Sports.content:
Alexander Isak and £35m goal machine will have Man Utd excited after last-minute deal

Chido Obi has joined Eredivisie side Willem II, following in the footsteps of £125million signing Alexander Isak and Manchester United have every reason to be excited for the future

View Image Chido Obi has left Man United on loan (Image: Getty Images)

Manchester United sealed a loan move for Chido Obi on deadline day, and the reflections of Alexander Isak and Benfica star Vangelis Pavlidis on their own breakthroughs at Willem II will give the club real optimism about his development. The 18‑year‑old joined the Dutch side after making eight senior appearances for United.

‌



Isak, who became a British transfer‑record signing when he joined Liverpool from Newcastle United for £125million last summer, spent a season on loan at Willem II from Borussia Dortmund after struggling for regular minutes in Germany. Arriving in Tilburg at 20, he described that spell as 'the most important season of my career', saying the pressure to deliver became the catalyst for everything that followed.

‌



He spoke about the value of minutes and how the club gave him the platform to prove himself when opportunities elsewhere were limited. "That season at Willem II was the most important season of my career," Isak previously said.

‌

Eight players Man Utd could lose for NOTHING with urgent talks planned READ MORE :

"Because that step, knowing I had to deliver, it's what made everything else possible. In football, you never know when the next chance is going to come, and so you take it.

"Obviously, as a young player, you need time on the pitch. If you're not getting that, all you can do is train harder... I knew my chance would come, even if it wasn't there, I knew it would come at another club and I wanted to be ready."

Greek forward Pavlidis followed a similar path, joining the Eredivisie side on loan from VfL Bochum at the age of 20. "Willem II was very important for my career," he recalled.

‌



"I was still looking for my position on the pitch, at that time I wasn't a number 9 yet. [So] to be at a club in the Eredivisie, to play and score goals in the league, to play the cup final, the European competitions, it was incredible."

Pavlidis went on to spend three years at AZ Alkmaar before making the switch to Lisbon to strengthen Portuguese giants Benfica in 2024. He has scored 71 goals in 118 Liga Portugal appearances to date.

‌



Earlier this summer, Pavlidis was linked with a Premier League move, with Tottenham and Aston Villa both reported to be interested in the striker. Serie A pair AC Milan and Roma also explored potential deals.

Barcelona were credited with an interest too, but Benfica made it clear they would only consider selling Pavlidis if an irresistible offer arrived. His release clause is set at €100m (£86m).

The Red Devils will be hoping for a similar success story with Chido, who is viewed internally as a star of the future. The teenager made his United debut against Tottenham in February 2025 and has eight senior appearances to his name.

He spent last season with the Under‑21s, scoring 15 goals in 31 matches, and has been a regular across multiple academy competitions - the EFL Trophy, National League Cup, FA Youth Cup, Premier League 2 and the International Under‑21s Cup.

United believe those fixtures have accelerated Obi's development and given him valuable experience ahead of his loan spell. The youngster arrived at Old Trafford in 2024 after spending four years in Arsenal's academy.

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Ogbene earns Republic of Ireland draw with Canada
Sports.content:
Chiedozie Ogbene's equaliser ensured the Republic of Ireland continued their good run of results as they drew 1-1 with World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal.

Canada went ahead in the 24th minute from an own goal by defender Jake O'Brien, heading a failed clearance into his own net from Stephen Eustaquio's corner.

Ireland were then awarded a penalty in the second half after Cyle Larin - who signed a two-year deal with Southampton earlier in the day - took out Jamie McGrath.

Canada goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau saved Troy Parrott's initial attempt, but Ogbene was on hand to slam home the rebound and tie the game in the 60th minute.

Image: Ireland's Jake O'Brien heads the ball into his own net

Ireland, who failed to qualify for this summer's World Cup, went close to a winner but Crepeau denied a charging run from Mason Melia late on.

The Orlando City goalkeeper missed out on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar after breaking his leg while playing in the MLS Cup final.

Canada, managed by former Leeds boss Jesse Marsch, officially open the World Cup on June 12 in Toronto against Bosnia and Herzegovina, before facing Qatar on June 18 and Switzerland on June 24.

They remain without captain Alphonso Davies, who is still nursing a hamstring injury he sustained while playing for Bayern Munich.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland edge past Qatar in friendly as both sides end with 10
Sports.content:
Captain Nathan Collins headed the Republic of Ireland to a 1-0 friendly victory over World Cup-bound Qatar as both sides were reduced to 10 men.

Collins ensured Ireland got the better of a side managed by his former Wolves boss Julen Lopetegui with an early header.

However, just how the evening might have panned out had Jack Moylan not been dismissed as half-time approached, a sparse crowd inside the Aviva Stadium will never know.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, whose hopes of making it to the World Cup finals were dashed in heartbreaking fashion in March when they lost their play-off semi-final to the Czech Republic on penalties, were in complete control until Moylan's premature exit.

Qatar substitute Almoez Ali suffered the same fate 12 minutes from time.

Image: Jack Moylan was sent off before half-time at the Aviva Stadium

The game was played out against the backdrop of ongoing unease at the forthcoming Nations League clashes with Israel, and play was interrupted on several occasions during the first half as 'Stop the Game' protesters among a crowd of 28,981 repeatedly hurled tennis balls on to the pitch.

Ireland will now head for Montreal and their friendly against World Cup co-hosts Canada on June 6, while Qatar continue their preparations for the finals - they launch their Group B campaign against Switzerland in San Francisco on June 13 - against El Salvador in Los Angeles on the same day.

The Republic took the lead with just five minutes gone when, having been fouled by Ayoub Al-Oui wide on the left, Moylan curled the resulting free-kick on to the head of Collins, who glanced the ball effortlessly past 'keeper Mahmoud Abunada.

Image: Qatar's Almoez Ali was also sent off

There was a brief interruption after the protesters made their presence felt for the first time as Qatar's Pedro Miguel underwent treatment for injury, but once order had been restored, Troy Parrott whipped a first-time shot wide after being picked out by Seamus Coleman.

The Qataris simply could not get anywhere near Hallgrimsson's men and a mid-half drinks break did little to improve matters for the visitors with Abunada having to field Jayson Molumby's deflected 24th-minute shot from distance.

Lopetegui could not hide his frustration on the sideline and only the bravery of defender Ahmed Fathi denied Chiedozie Ogbene a second goal as he attempted to latch on to Liam Scales' header back across goal.

But the home side's night took a turn for the worse on the stroke of half-time when Northern Irish referee Jamie Robinson deemed Moylan's challenge on Jassem Gaber worthy of a red card, much to the Lincoln frontman's clear astonishment.

Image: Former Wolves and West Ham boss Julen Lopetegui is now in charge of Qatar

With defender James Abankwah having replaced Dara O'Shea at half-time, the 10 men found themselves under pressure for the first time on their return, although Coleman very nearly caught Abunada off his line with an audacious 52nd-minute attempt from the right wing.

Edmilson Junior dragged a long-range effort wide two minutes later after Molumby went down in midfield under Fathi's challenge and it took a fine 71st-minute reaction save by Caoimhin Kelleher - his first of the night - to keep out Yusuf Abdurisag's deflected shot.

However, Qatari hopes of salvation were dashed with 12 minutes remaining when Ali struck out at Molumby off the ball on several occasions and was also sent off.

Sports.title: Parrott out of luck as Republic of Ireland draw with North Macedonia
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott had two goals disallowed as the Republic of Ireland played out a stalemate against North Macedonia on the night on which they had hoped to book a trip to the World Cup finals.

Five days after their dreams came to an end for another four years in Prague, Ireland drew 0-0 with the Macedonians in a friendly encounter neither side wanted as the Czech Republic and Denmark fought for the big prize.

Even a third successive home victory for the first time since the 2015-16 campaign would have provided scant consolation for Thursday night's disappointment but Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had to make do with a disappointing draw.

AZ Alkmaar striker Parrott came closest to breaking the deadlock as 37-year-old defender Seamus Coleman received a standing ovation from a crowd of 39,560 at the Aviva Stadium when he was replaced during the second half of what could yet prove to be his final appearance for his country.

Nevertheless, the squad will reconvene for a series of friendlies at the end of the season ahead of next season's Nations League campaign and later Euro 2028 qualification having restored a measure of pride and established a momentum they hope will serve them well when they return to competitive action.

The hosts went on to the offensive from the off, although they were unable to find the final ball to allow either Parrott or Chiedozie Ogbene to threaten.

John Egan could not direct an 11th-minute corner at goal and Ogbene saw his snapshot deflected over three minutes later, but goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher had to parry Enis Bardhi's 21st-minute free-kick after it flicked off the defensive wall, with Bardhi volleying high over after the resulting corner had been only half-cleared.

Macedonia keeper Stole Dimitrievski saved Parrott's 23rd-minute header comfortably after Dara O'Shea and Finn Azaz had sparked a concerted attack, and Azaz failed to make the most of a free-kick two minutes later after he had been tripped just outside the penalty area.

Parrott was played into a promising position by Knight nine minutes before the break, only to miss the target by some distance.

The in-form striker - he scored his sixth goal in three games in Prague - might have done better again two minutes later after Azaz's clipped pass had caused problems for the Macedonian defence but he snatched at his attempt and fired high and wide.

Parrott twice had the ball in the net as time ran down but an offside flag stalled his celebrations on each occasion.

Ireland were unfortunate not to take the lead with 52 minutes gone when Azaz accepted Seamus Coleman's pass and found Parrott, who turned smartly before shooting against the upright.

Azaz curled an effort just wide and Tihomir Kostadinov denied Parrott a clear run on goal as the hosts began to turn the screw but it was veteran Coleman's 61st-minute departure as

Hallgrimsson made changes which attracted the biggest cheer of the night to that point.

Wholesale changes did not help the flow of the game, which rather petered out as the whistle approached, although Ireland substitute Johnny Kenny passed up a glorious opportunity to win it at the end with a weak shot at the keeper.

Sports.title: Szmodics out of hospital and 'on the mend' after collision
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics has been released from hospital in Prague after being knocked unconscious during Thursday's World Cup play-off defeat by the Czech Republic.

The 24-year-old, who is currently on loan at Derby from Ipswich, was hurt in a collision with defender Stepan Chaloupek just two minutes after his introduction as an extra-time substitute at the Fortuna Arena, sparking concerned medics to rush to his aid.

Szmodics was carried from the field on a stretcher and taken straight to hospital, where Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later revealed he would spend the night under observation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan looks back on the heartbreaking result for the Republic of Ireland who lost their World Cup qualifying play-off against Czech Republic on penalties

A Football Association of Ireland spokesperson said on Friday morning: "Sammie Szmodics was transferred to hospital yesterday having sustained a head injury during extra time of the play-off against Czechia.

"Following further tests and a period of observation, he has been safely discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery under the care of the Republic of Ireland and Derby County medical teams."

Szmodics, who Hallgrimsson confirmed would have taken a penalty in the shoot-out which Ireland ultimately lost 4-3, took to social media to express his thanks to those who had helped him.

He posted on X: "Gutted the way it ended. Fans and boys immense all evening!! Appreciate everyone's messages. And thank you to the medical staff who acted so quickly to help me. On the mend."
