The Final Tally

By early September, InfoMoney reported the full month’s total: a net outflow of 18.1 billion reais (US$3.5 billion). It called this the worst month for foreign investors in all of 2026.

The gap between InfoMoney’s estimates shows how B3 data shifts as more trading days close. The final total still marked the deepest monthly loss of the year.

A Rough Start, Then a Reversal

Early in August, foreign investors sold heavily, pulling out about 23 billion reais (US$4.4 billion) by 20 August. CNN Brasil reported that outflow using B3 data through that date.

After that, roughly 5 billion reais (US$1.0 billion) flowed back in during the rest of the month, CNN Brasil said. That reversal trimmed the final outflow to about 18 billion reais (US$3.5 billion).

One Day Turned Positive

Not every day in August was negative for foreign investors. On 27 August alone, B3 data showed a net inflow of 208 million reais (US$40 million).

That single day of buying was small next to the month’s losses. But it hinted at the partial recovery that followed in late August.

Why Foreign Investors Sold

Analysts pointed to caution ahead of Brazil’s elections and worries about the government’s fiscal plans. Money Times reported that JPMorgan and Morgan Stanley both grew more cautious on Brazilian shares in August.

Both banks cited a slowing economy and rising credit risks in their notes. Those views likely fed into the foreign selling that outlets tracked through the month.

The Ibovespa’s Bumpy August

Brazil’s benchmark stock index, the Ibovespa, actually fell about 0.3 percent in August 2026, InfoMoney reported. That is a small move, but it followed a wild month for foreign investors.

The index fell for 11 straight sessions from 4 to 18 August, tracking the heaviest foreign selling. It then rose for nine sessions in a row into September, InfoMoney said.

Not the First Swing This Year

August was not the first month with unusual foreign flows in 2026. In July, foreign investors added 4.3 billion reais (US$0.8 billion) to Brazilian shares, InfoMoney reported.

Earlier in 2026, foreign investors had also poured large sums into Brazilian shares, especially in January, according to Money Times.

A Record Streak of Selling

The consultancy Elos Ayta tracks B3’s foreign investor data back to January 2022. ADVFN reported that August’s outflow became one of the two largest in that entire record, alongside May 2026.

Einar Rivero, the consultancy’s founder, compiled the analysis using B3’s own trading data. It excluded new share offerings, focusing only on shares already listed on the exchange.

Foreign Investors’ Role on B3

Foreign investors have long been one of the biggest groups trading shares on B3. That is why their August retreat drew so much attention from Brazilian financial media.

When foreign investors sell heavily, it can weigh on share prices even if local buyers step in. Their August exit tested how much the market could rely on domestic demand alone.

The Brazilian Real

The US dollar closed at about 5.18 reais on 31 August 2026, according to CNN Brasil and InfoMoney. That is a reference point for the size of these flows.

A weaker real can make imports pricier for Brazilians and change returns for foreign investors. Currency moves depend on many factors, not just stock flows.

What Comes Next

Investors will watch whether foreign investors keep selling or return to buying in September. Early September data already showed the Ibovespa extending its winning streak.

If foreign investors come back, it could support further gains in Brazilian shares. If they keep selling, the rally may depend more on local buyers.

Background on B3

B3 is Brazil’s main stock exchange and clearing house, based in São Paulo. It lists shares of the country’s largest companies and publishes daily investor flow data.

Brazilian and international media routinely summarize this data. Because B3 updates its figures as more trades settle, early estimates often change once a full month closes.

Methodology Differences

B3’s own daily data, InfoMoney’s tallies, and JPMorgan’s bank research are three different ways to measure the same trend. Each uses a different cut-off date or counting method.

That is why one report said 18.4 billion reais and another said 22 billion reais for roughly the same period. Both describe real selling by foreign investors, just measured differently.

Sources and Verification

This article relies on reporting from InfoMoney, CNN Brasil, ADVFN News, Money Times, and Revista Oeste, all citing B3 or JPMorgan data. Figures for August varied slightly by date and methodology.

The final, most complete figure for August is InfoMoney’s 18.1 billion reais (US$3.5 billion) total. That is the number this article treats as most reliable.

Frequently Asked Questions

How much did foreign investors pull from Brazilian shares in August 2026?

Foreign investors withdrew about 18.1 billion reais (US$3.5 billion) from Brazilian shares in August 2026, according to InfoMoney. That made it the worst month of the year.

Why did foreign investors sell Brazilian shares in August 2026?

Analysts pointed to caution before Brazil’s elections and fiscal worries. Money Times reported that JPMorgan and Morgan Stanley both grew more cautious on Brazilian shares.

Did the Ibovespa fall because foreign investors were selling?

The Ibovespa dipped about 0.3 percent in August, then rallied for nine straight sessions into September. Foreign selling likely contributed to the index’s rough start to the month.

What is B3?

B3 is Brazil’s main stock exchange and clearing house. It publishes daily data on investor flows, including how much foreign investors buy and sell.

Colombia · INFRASTRUCTURE

Key Facts — What happened Bogota’s city government reactivated the international tender for Metro Line 2.

— The deadline Groups must submit for the Line 2 tender by Monday, 7 September 2026, La República reported.

— How big The contract award is targeted for 2027, before construction starts.

— The catch Line 2 is still in planning, not construction; Line 1 is being built.

— Who it hits Commuters in Bogota, who await an expanded metro network.

— What comes next Interested parties will be announced in the coming days, says the president.

Groups bidding to build Bogota’s Metro Line 2 face a Monday deadline, La República reports. It is the next step since the city’s first tender for the line failed.

The first train for the Bogota metro. Line 1 is under construction while Line 2 goes back out to tender. (Photo: The Rio Times archive.)

Groups bidding to build Bogota’s metro line 2 must submit by Monday, 7 September 2026, La República reported. The city government aims to award the contract in 2027.

Tender Restart

Groups bidding for Bogota’s Metro Line 2 must submit their offers by Monday, 7 September 2026, La República reported. This closes the second round of an international tender for the line.

Bogota’s first Metro Line 2 tender was declared void in January 2026, after no group submitted a final offer. The city government reopened the international tender in February 2026, Infobae reported.

The goal is to award the contract in 2027, before construction begins. The city is seeking broader participation from international firms.

President’s Statement

On 2 September 2026, President Abelardo De La Espriella visited the Bogota Metro and said the structuring is in its final stage. He added that interested parties will be known in the coming days.

La República reported his words. “The structuring is entering its final stage,” he said.

He added that the interested parties in the tender would be known in the coming days.

Current Status of Metro Lines

Metro Line 2 is still in planning, not construction. Lines 2 and 3 are in structuring phases, while Line 1 is under construction.

President De La Espriella has committed to finishing Line 1 and advancing Lines 2 and 3. He also mentioned structuring studies for a future Line 4.

Why the First Attempt Failed

The first Line 2 tender closed with no valid offers, so the city declared it void in January 2026, Infobae reported. The prequalified groups did not submit final proposals by the deadline.

The city government then reopened the process to attract more international companies. It is now working to ensure a successful second tender.

Timeline and Next Steps

Offers for the Line 2 tender are due Monday, 7 September 2026, according to La República. The contract award is still targeted for 2027.

Interested parties will be revealed in the coming days, the president said. This report does not name any bidders.

Political Context

President De La Espriella has made the metro a priority. His promises include finishing Line 1 and pushing forward Lines 2 and 3.

This political support adds pressure but does not change the formal tender calendar. The city government leads the process.

International Participation

The city is seeking to expand participation from international firms. This is part of the reactivated tender process.

More international interest could bring expertise and competition. The city hopes this will lead to a successful award.

Funding and Costs

No verified contract value for Line 2 has been disclosed. Reports do not provide cost estimates for the new tender.

The national and Bogota governments do have a co-financing deal for the metro network as a whole. Its size has not been confirmed for this article.

Technical Details Unknown

Line 2 is planned to run 15.5 kilometers, with 11 stations. Ten stations will be underground and one elevated, according to the Bogota city government and Empresa Metro de Bogota.

The line will also have one maintenance yard, in the Fontanar del Rio area. These figures come from official city planning documents, not the new tender itself.

Challenges Ahead

The tender process faces challenges, including ensuring transparency and attracting qualified bidders. The city must also manage public expectations.

The failed first attempt adds pressure to get this right. A successful tender is crucial for Bogota’s metro expansion.

Public Expectations

Residents of Bogota have long awaited an expanded metro system. Line 1 is under construction, but Lines 2 and 3 are still years away.

The reactivated tender brings hope for progress. However, the timeline remains uncertain.

What to Watch

Watch for the announcement of interested parties in the coming days. This will show which companies are competing.

Also watch for the tender schedule and any official notices. The city has not yet published a detailed timeline.

Conclusion

Bogota’s metro line 2 tender is back on track after a failed first attempt. The city aims to award the contract in 2027.

The coming days will reveal interested parties, marking a key step. The process remains in early stages.

What the President Said

On 2 September 2026, President Abelardo De La Espriella said the structuring of Line 2 is entering its final stage. He added that ‘in the coming days the interested parties in the tender will be known.’

This quote was reported by La República. It shows the president’s direct involvement in the project’s progress.

The Failed First Attempt

The current tender process is a second try. The first attempt was declared void in January 2026, according to Infobae, after no group submitted a final offer.

The city government reopened the international tender in February 2026. They now aim to attract more international companies.

Who Is in Charge

The Bogotá city government, known as the Alcaldía de Bogotá, is leading the tender. They are the authority that reactivated the process.

The president supports the project but does not run the tender. The city government will make the final contract award.

What Happens Next

The stated goal is to award the Line 2 contract in 2027, according to Infobae and El Espectador.

Before that, the city will reveal interested parties in the coming days. Then they will proceed with the formal tender steps.

Other Metro Lines

President De La Espriella also promised to finish Line 1 and push forward Lines 2 and 3. He wants to start studying a future Line 4.

This was reported by La República and Infobae on 2 September 2026. Lines 2 and 3 are still in planning, not construction.

What Is Not Known Yet

This report does not name the bidders for the Line 2 tender. The groups that dropped out of the failed first tender are also not named here, to avoid unfair blame.

No contract value for Line 2 has been disclosed yet. That figure should emerge once the city picks a winner.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the status of Bogota’s Metro Line 2 tender?

The tender has been reactivated after a failed first attempt. The city government is leading the process and aims to award the contract in 2027.

When will interested parties be announced?

President Abelardo De La Espriella said on 2 September 2026 that interested parties will be known in the coming days. The structuring is in its final stage.

Is Metro Line 2 under construction?

No, Metro Line 2 is still in planning. Only Line 1 is under construction, while Lines 2 and 3 are in structuring phases.

Why did the first tender attempt fail?

No group submitted a final offer, so the city declared the tender void in January 2026, Infobae reported. The city reopened the process to attract more international firms.

Sources: Infobae; La República; El Espectador.

Chile · ECONOMY

Key Facts — What happened Chile’s central bank survey shows traders expect the key rate at 4.5% for two years.

— How big The policy rate is 4.5%, held since December 2025.

— The catch The bank has not committed to two years; it’s only a market expectation.

— Who it hits Borrowers and businesses face stable loan costs for now.

— What comes next No change is expected at the September 8 meeting.

Market operators in Chile expect the central bank to keep its benchmark interest rate unchanged for the next two years. The forecast comes from the bank’s own survey of financial operators.

Chile’s key rate is expected to stay at 4.5% for the next two years, according to a central bank survey. The forecast comes from financial operators polled by the Banco Central de Chile.

Survey Shows Long Hold

On September 3, 2026, Chile’s central bank published its survey of financial operators. The operators projected that the key rate would remain at 4.5% for a 24-month horizon.

Reuters reported the same day that traders expect the central bank to hold its benchmark rate for two years. The survey is called the Encuesta de Operadores Financieros.

Current Policy Rate

The TPM is the interest rate the central bank charges on short-term loans to commercial banks. It influences borrowing costs for consumers and businesses throughout Chile.

The TPM has been at 4.5% since December 2025. The central bank’s board unanimously decided to hold it at that level again in late July 2026.

No Change Expected at Next Meeting

The survey also showed that operators do not expect any change at the upcoming monetary policy meeting on September 8, 2026. This is consistent with the central bank’s own signals.

Financial operators, not the central bank, expect the rate to stay this way for a good while. The central bank itself says it will decide meeting by meeting, citing an uncertain macroeconomic environment.

Inflation Forecasts

Operators in the survey forecast annual inflation of 3.3% over the next 12 months. That is below the central bank’s 3% target but not at it.

The central bank’s own forecast, from its June 2026 Monetary Policy Report, sees headline inflation closing 2026 at about 4.2%. It expects inflation to return to the 3% target in the second quarter of 2027.

Growth Outlook

The same report revised down Chile’s GDP growth forecast for 2026 to a range of 1.0% to 1.75%. This reflects a weak first quarter, hit by lower copper ore grades and weaker farming and tourism activity.

The central bank has acknowledged that the economy has grown less than expected. This weak growth is one reason why the bank is cautious about cutting rates.

Why the Rate Stays Put

The central bank has kept the TPM at 4.5% since December 2025. It has emphasized that the macroeconomic environment faces an unusual degree of uncertainty.

Geopolitical risks, such as the Middle East conflict, add to that uncertainty. The bank prefers to wait for clearer signs before changing rates.

What This Means for Borrowers

For people with mortgages or business loans, a stable key rate means their borrowing costs are unlikely to change soon. Banks often adjust their own rates based on the central bank’s policy rate.

If the key rate stays at 4.5% for two years, loan rates may remain relatively steady. That could help households and companies plan their finances.

Survey Details

The survey of financial operators is a regular poll conducted by the central bank. It asks banks, brokers, and other financial institutions about their expectations for the economy.

The results are used by the central bank as one input for its policy decisions. They also give the public a view of what market participants think will happen.

Market Reaction

The news of the expected long hold was reported by La Tercera’s Pulso section and Reuters. It did not cause major market movements, as the expectation was already widespread.

The Chilean peso and local bonds showed little change after the survey was published. Investors had already priced in a prolonged hold.

Central Bank’s Stance

In its July meeting, the central bank’s board chose to keep the TPM at 4.5% for the fifth consecutive time. It noted that the macroeconomic scenario remains subject to greater uncertainty than usual.

The bank has signaled that it will not rush to cut rates. It wants to see more evidence that inflation is under control.

Potential Future Moves

Some economists expect a possible 25-point cut late in 2026 or early 2027. But the survey suggests that most operators see no change for two years.

The central bank has not committed to any specific path. Its decisions will depend on how inflation and growth evolve.

Inflation Data

Chile’s annual inflation in July 2026 stood at 3.5%. That is within the central bank’s tolerance range but above its 3% target.

Inflation has stayed above the bank’s 3% target for months. The bank is watching for clearer signs it is coming down before it changes rates.

Economic Context

Chile’s economy has been growing slowly, with GDP growth forecast at only 1.0% to 1.75% for 2026. High fuel prices and weak consumer confidence have added to the challenges.

The central bank faces a delicate balance between supporting growth and controlling inflation. Keeping rates steady is its current approach.

What to Watch

The next monetary policy meeting is on September 8, 2026. No change is expected, but the bank’s statement will be watched for any new signals.

Investors will also monitor upcoming inflation data and economic activity reports. These could influence the central bank’s decisions later this year.

Understanding the Key Rate

The TPM is Chile’s main interest rate, set by the Banco Central de Chile. It influences borrowing costs for banks and consumers.

A 4.5% rate means the central bank charges commercial banks 4.5% interest on short-term loans.

This rate affects mortgages, car loans, and business credit. High rates make borrowing costlier, slowing spending and inflation.

The central bank has kept it at 4.5% since December 2025, per La Tercera.

Survey Process and Participants

The Encuesta de Operadores Financieros is a regular survey by the Banco Central de Chile. It asks financial operators, such as traders and analysts, about their expectations for the economy.

The survey is conducted before each monetary policy meeting.

The results are published and help the central bank gauge market sentiment. On September 3, 2026, La Tercera reported that operators expected no change at the September 8 meeting.

The survey also projected a 0.3% monthly CPI increase for September, as noted in the same report.

Recent Economic Data

Chile’s economy shows mixed signals. The Imacec activity index fell 1.5% year-on-year in July 2026, per El Clarín on September 1, 2026.

This points to weak activity, and the central bank forecasts 2026 GDP growth at only 1.0% to 1.75%.

Inflation has been above the 3% target. July 2026 annual inflation was 3.5%, as reported by El Clarín on September 1, 2026.

The central bank expects inflation to close 2026 at about 4.2%. It will return to 3% only in Q2 2027, per the June IPoM.

Central Bank’s Communication

The central bank signaled caution in its July 2026 meeting. It noted ‘a degree of uncertainty greater than usual,’ as reported by La Tercera on August 28, 2026.

This suggests wariness of geopolitical risks and economic volatility.

The bank has flagged inflation worries and prefers to move cautiously. This communication aids market understanding, but it does not commit to a specific future path.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is Chile’s key rate?

Chile’s key rate, or TPM, is the interest rate the central bank charges on short-term loans to commercial banks. It influences borrowing costs across the economy.

Why is the key rate expected to stay at 4.5%?

The central bank’s survey of financial operators shows they expect no change for two years. This is based on inflation forecasts around 3.3% and weak growth.

When is the next central bank meeting?

The next monetary policy meeting is on September 8, 2026. The survey suggests no change will be made at that meeting.

Will the central bank cut rates soon?

The central bank itself has not promised this. But most operators in its own survey expect no cut for two years, though some economists see a possible small cut in late 2026 or early 2027.

Sources: La Tercera; Reuters; Diario Estrategia; El Clarín.

World.title: Nvidia Buys Hugging Face in a US$12.93 Billion Deal
World.content:
Technology · DEALS

Key Facts — What happened Nvidia signed a definitive agreement to buy Hugging Face for US$12.93 billion.

— How big The price is about US$13 billion, as Bloomberg reported.

— The catch The deal is signed but not closed, and it still needs regulatory approval.

— Who it hits Developers in Latin America who build on open models will watch closely.

— What comes next Hugging Face will stay an open platform, Nvidia says.

The chip giant will pay US$12.93 billion for the open-source AI hub. The deal keeps Hugging Face open for developers.

Nvidia Buys Hugging Face in a US$12.93 Billion Deal. (Photo: The Rio Times archive.)

Nvidia buys Hugging Face, the open-source AI platform, for US$12.93 billion. The deal was announced on 3 September 2026.

The Deal

Nvidia, the world’s leading maker of AI chips, has agreed to buy the platform. The price is US$12.93 billion, according to Reuters and Yahoo Finance.

Bloomberg put the value at about US$13 billion. That figure includes an up to US$1 billion equity-based retention program for the platform employees who join Nvidia.

What Hugging Face Does

Hugging Face is a popular developer platform for artificial intelligence. It hosts open-source AI models and datasets.

Open-source AI models are programs that anyone can use, modify, and share. Developers use them to build their own AI applications without starting from scratch.

Why Nvidia Wants It

Nvidia is betting that support for open AI models will drive future demand. Even as its biggest customers develop their own chips, Nvidia wants to stay central to AI development.

By owning the platform, Nvidia gains a key hub where developers gather. This strengthens its position across the AI stack, from chips to software.

The Price Breakdown

Under the deal, Nvidia will pay about US$11.9 billion to the platform investors. It will offer up to US$1 billion in equity-based retention for employees who join Nvidia.

Fox Business reported the same figures, based on Nvidia’s own filing. CNBC and TechCrunch also confirmed the US$12.93 billion price.

Hugging Face Stays Open

Nvidia says the platform will continue operating under its existing brand. It will remain an open, multi-cloud platform.

Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang said the platform “will remain an open platform for the entire AI ecosystem”.

He said developers would keep choosing their own models, frameworks, clouds and computing platforms.

Regulatory Hurdles

The deal still needs regulatory approval before it can close. Nvidia expects to complete the purchase in the first half of 2027, Fox Business and The Register reported.

Government reviews are common for big technology purchases. Nvidia’s size in AI chips means this deal could draw extra scrutiny.

Impact on Latin American Developers

Many developers in Latin America build on open-source AI models from Hugging Face. They use these tools to create local language models and applications.

If the deal closes, these developers will watch to see if Hugging Face truly remains open. Nvidia’s promise is key to their continued trust.

Nvidia’s Share Reaction

Nvidia shares edged up slightly after the announcement, Yahoo Finance reported. The move was small, since investors had expected the deal for days.

Investors welcomed the acquisition as strengthening Nvidia’s position across the AI stack.

Background of the Talks

On 2 September 2026, Bloomberg reported Nvidia was in advanced talks to buy Hugging Face. The deal was expected to total about US$14 billion including retention.

Earlier, on 27 August 2026, The Information reported Nvidia had agreed in principle to buy Hugging Face for US$12.9 billion. Other outlets said the deal was not yet signed and could still fall through.

Hugging Face’s Valuation History

Hugging Face was valued at US$4.5 billion in its 2023 funding round. In late 2025, a proposed Nvidia investment at a US$7 billion valuation was rejected.

The current deal price of US$12.93 billion is nearly three times the 2023 valuation.

Revenue Multiples

Hugging Face had annualized revenue of about US$150 million, according to TechCrunch and other reports. That means Nvidia paid roughly 86 times revenue for the platform.

This is a high price for the revenue, but Nvidia is betting on Hugging Face’s reach among developers, not its current sales.

What Developers Should Know

Hugging Face says its platform serves over 18 million developers. It hosts more than 3 million models and 500,000 datasets, according to Nvidia’s own announcement.

Developers should watch the regulatory process. The deal is signed but not yet closed.

What Comes Next

The deal is expected to close after regulatory approvals. Nvidia plans to keep Hugging Face as an open platform.

For now, developers can continue using Hugging Face as before. The future depends on the deal’s completion.

What Is Hugging Face?

Hugging Face is a platform where developers share and use open-source AI models and datasets. It is often described as a central hub for the AI community, similar to GitHub for code.

The platform supports open AI models, meaning anyone can access and modify them. This makes it a key part of the open-source AI ecosystem, which contrasts with proprietary models from companies like OpenAI.

What Is Nvidia?

Nvidia is a major technology company known for making computer chips, especially graphics processing units (GPUs). These chips are essential for training and running AI models, giving Nvidia a dominant position in the AI hardware market.

Nvidia’s Hugging Face purchase expands it beyond hardware into software and platforms.

This move strengthens its role across the AI stack, from chips to developer tools.

What Does the Price Mean in Everyday Terms?

The deal is worth US$12.93 billion, which is a huge amount of money. To put it in perspective, that is more than the gross domestic product of some small countries, like Iceland or Luxembourg.

Nvidia will pay about US$11.9 billion to Hugging Face’s investors, and up to US$1 billion in stock to employees who join Nvidia. This means the total value includes both cash and stock incentives.

What Happened Before the Announcement?

Before the deal, Hugging Face was valued at US$4.5 billion in a 2023 funding round. In late 2025, Nvidia reportedly considered investing at a US$7 billion valuation, but that deal was rejected.

In late August 2026, reports emerged that Nvidia agreed in principle to buy Hugging Face for US$12.9 billion. The agreement was not yet signed and could still collapse.

The final deal was announced on September 3, 2026.

What Are the Next Steps?

The deal is subject to regulatory approvals, which are typical for large technology acquisitions. This means government agencies in the United States and possibly Europe will review the deal to ensure it does not harm competition.

Nvidia has said that Hugging Face will continue to operate under its existing brand as an open, multi-cloud platform. This suggests that the platform will remain available to developers across different cloud providers, not just Nvidia’s own services.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is Hugging Face?

Hugging Face is a platform that hosts open-source AI models and datasets. Developers use it to build AI applications.

How much is Nvidia paying for Hugging Face?

Nvidia is paying US$12.93 billion. Bloomberg reported the value as about US$13 billion.

Will Hugging Face remain open after the acquisition?

Nvidia says yes. Hugging Face will continue as an open, multi-cloud platform.

When will the deal close?

The deal needs regulatory approval. Nvidia expects it to close in the first half of 2027.

Sources: Reuters; Bloomberg; CNBC; TechCrunch; Yahoo Finance; Fox Business; Nvidia.

World.title: Ecopetrol Says a Community Is Holding Up Sirius Gas
World.content:
Colombia · ENERGY

Key Facts — What happened Ecopetrol accused a community of extortion in talks over the Sirius gas project.

— Who said it Elsa Jaimes, Ecopetrol’s general manager for offshore and exploration, made the allegation on September 2.

— The catch The community publicly rejected the accusation the next day; no payment amount has been disclosed by either side.

— Why it matters The dispute could delay first gas from Sirius, Colombia’s largest offshore gas find.

— What comes next Ecopetrol aims to finish community consultations by end-2026 and sanction the project in 2027.

Colombia’s state oil company says a coastal community is holding up its biggest offshore gas project with demands it calls extortion; the community rejects that.

A semi-submersible drilling rig at a shipyard. Ecopetrol says one community’s demands threaten the Sirius gas project. (Photo: The Rio Times archive.)

Colombia’s state oil company Ecopetrol says a community’s financial demands amount to extortion and threaten the Sirius gas project. The extortion claim came from Elsa Jaimes, Ecopetrol’s general manager for offshore and exploration, on September 2.

Ecopetrol’s Extortion Claim

Ecopetrol, Colombia’s state-controlled oil company, has accused a coastal community near Santa Marta of extortion during talks over the Sirius gas project. The accusation came from Elsa Jaimes, Ecopetrol’s general manager for offshore and exploration, on September 2.

Jaimes said the community was asking for a lot of money. She described the situation as being ‘at the level of extortion,’ according to El Tiempo, a leading Colombian newspaper.

What Is the Sirius Field

Sirius is described by Colombian media as the country’s largest offshore gas discovery, located in the Caribbean Sea. It is being developed by Ecopetrol with partner Petrobras.

Colombia is relying on Sirius and other Caribbean fields to offset falling gas output from existing sources. Without new supply, the country risks a gas shortfall in the coming years.

Colombia currently gets most of its gas from Piedemonte Llanero and the Chuchupa-Ballena fields in La Guajira. Getting Sirius gas to those inland markets will also need new pipeline infrastructure.

The Exploration and Production segment engages in the exploration and production of oil and gas. The Transport and Logistics segment is involved in…

The Prior Consultation Process

Colombian law requires a prior consultation process with communities affected by major projects. This process, known as consulta previa, aims to protect the rights of ethnic and local groups.

Ecopetrol must reach agreements with all certified communities before it can seek an environmental licence for the gas pipeline. The company says it has started dialogue with 97% of these communities.

The pipeline that would carry Sirius gas ashore runs about 117 kilometres. Colombia’s national prior-consultation authority certifies which communities along that route must be consulted.

The Disputed Demand

A Petrobras Colombia executive said the community was seeking a payment 20 times larger than what 116 other communities had requested. Alcindo Moritz, president of Petrobras Colombia, said the companies could not remain ‘hostage’ to such a demand.

Neither Ecopetrol nor Petrobras disclosed the exact amount requested. El Tiempo reported that Jaimes did not reveal the sum.

Project Timeline at Risk

Ecopetrol and Petrobras plan to complete prior consultations by the end of 2026. They aim to request the gas pipeline’s environmental licence in the first quarter of 2027.

The partners expect to sanction project execution by the end of 2027. Delays in the consultation process could push back these dates.

First Gas Expected Around 2030

Ecopetrol’s public statements point to first gas from Sirius around 2030. The company has acknowledged this could slip to 2031.

No gas is currently flowing from Sirius; the field is still in the licensing and development stage. The extortion dispute adds uncertainty to that already tight schedule.

The Community Rejects the Accusation

The community answered back the day after Ecopetrol’s allegation. A leader of the community’s indigenous council, David Cantillo, called the extortion framing unfair on 3 September 2026.

Cantillo said the community was only defending its territorial and cultural rights under Colombia’s prior consultation law. He said the community’s presence in the project area had already been documented by Colombia’s own prior-consultation authority.

Cantillo also pointed to research on how earlier gas projects affected Indigenous communities in La Guajira. He said that history was why his community wanted stronger guarantees before agreeing to Sirius.

Progress With Other Communities

Ecopetrol says it has made progress with most other communities in the consultation process. It reports that 38 communities, or 32% of the total, have already signed agreements.

This suggests the dispute over one community’s demand is a bottleneck, not a system-wide failure. The company is pushing to resolve it quickly.

Legal and Regulatory Hurdles

The dispute sits inside the environmental licensing process for the gas pipeline. Ecopetrol says that without a signed agreement it cannot advance its application before Colombia’s National Environmental Licensing Authority, known as ANLA.

ANLA is the Colombian agency that approves environmental licences for major projects. Its approval is essential for the Sirius pipeline to move forward.

Ecopetrol’s Position

Ecopetrol and Petrobras executives argue the project cannot be held back by what they call a disproportionate demand. They say they remain committed to dialogue but will not accept what they describe as extortion.

That description is an allegation from the companies, not a proven fact. No court or regulator has ruled on the matter.

What’s at Stake for Colombia

Sirius is seen as important for Colombia’s energy security. The country’s existing gas fields are ageing, and imported gas is costly.

A delay in the project could push Colombia to rely more on imports. That could raise gas costs for households and industry.

Next Steps

Ecopetrol and Petrobras must resolve the dispute to keep prior consultation on schedule. They have set themselves until the end of 2026 to complete it.

If they fail, the timeline for first gas could slip further. The extortion claim and the community’s rejection of it have both put the negotiation under public scrutiny.

A One-Sided Dispute So Far

Colombia’s national government has not issued a public statement on Ecopetrol’s extortion allegation. ANLA has also stayed silent on the specific dispute so far.

That leaves the disagreement between the company and the community as the main public account so far. Both sides now have their competing claims on the record, but neither has offered documentary proof.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the Sirius gas project?

Sirius is described as Colombia’s largest offshore gas discovery, in the Caribbean Sea. It is being developed by Ecopetrol with partner Petrobras.

What is prior consultation in Colombia?

Prior consultation is a legal process to seek agreement with communities affected by major projects. It is called consulta previa in Spanish.

Why did Ecopetrol accuse a community of extortion?

A Petrobras Colombia executive said the community was demanding a payment 20 times larger than 116 other communities. Ecopetrol’s Elsa Jaimes called the situation ‘at the level of extortion.’

Did the community respond to the accusation?

Yes. A leader of its indigenous council rejected the claim on 3 September 2026 and said the community was defending its consultation rights.

When will Sirius produce first gas?

Ecopetrol expects first gas around 2030, but says it could slip to 2031. The timeline depends on resolving community consultations.

Sources: El Tiempo (Colombia); Infobae Colombia; Seguimiento.co.

World.title: Milei Joins the Madrid Forum in Santiago and Meets Kast
World.content:
Argentina · POLITICS

Key Facts — What happened Milei flew to Santiago on September 3, 2026, for the Madrid Forum.

— How big The forum gathered over 40 speakers from 25 countries.

— The catch The bilateral with Kast was their fourth meeting in under a year.

— Who it hits The event strengthens ties among conservative leaders in the Americas.

— What comes next Milei returned to Buenos Aires the same day after the meeting.

Argentine President Javier Milei travels to Santiago for a right-wing forum and talks with Chilean President José Antonio Kast.

Javier Milei speaking at a Vox event. The Madrid Forum is run by Fundacion Disenso, the Spanish party’s think tank. (Photo: The Rio Times archive.)

Argentine President Javier Milei made a brief Chile visit on September 3, 2026. He spoke at the Madrid Forum and met President José Antonio Kast in Santiago.

A Quick Trip South

Javier Milei left Buenos Aires at 07:00 on Thursday, September 3, 2026, for a short trip to Chile. His plane landed in Santiago, where he attended the Madrid Forum and held a bilateral meeting with President José Antonio Kast.

The Argentine president spoke at the forum at 09:30 at the Centro de Eventos San Carlos de Apoquindo. He then went to La Moneda, the presidential palace, for meetings.

The Madrid Forum in Santiago

The Madrid Forum is a right-wing political initiative linked to Fundación Disenso, a think tank tied to Spain’s Vox party. This was its fifth regional meeting, held in Santiago on September 3 and 4, 2026.

The event gathered over 40 speakers from 25 countries. Its motto was ‘A new era for Ibero-America’.

Kast gave the opening speech, then Milei spoke.

Who Attended and Organized

Fundación Disenso organized the forum, which is part of a network of conservative and far-right politicians from Europe and the Americas. José Antonio Kast, Chile’s president, is an original signatory of the Madrid Charter, a document promoting conservative values.

The forum also included other regional leaders and figures from the right-wing bloc. The event aimed to strengthen cooperation among like-minded governments.

The Bilateral Meeting with Kast

After the forum Milei met Sarah Rogers, a United States State Department official, at La Moneda. Rogers is the Under Secretary of State for Public Diplomacy.

Around midday he held a bilateral meeting with President Kast. Chilean outlets gave the time as 11:30, while one Argentine outlet gave it as noon.

This was their fourth face-to-face meeting in under a year, according to Argentine outlets El Cronista and Canal 26. The talks focused on regional issues and bilateral relations, though no specific agreements were announced.

Background of the Visit

The trip came during tension over the Magellan Strait and separate questions about Milei aide Fernando Cerimedo, Argentine and Chilean media reported. These issues sat in the background of the visit, not its main focus.

Milei’s forum participation aligns Argentina with right-wing and libertarian networks. He had previously met with Kast and with Vox leaders.

Reactions and Criticism

The forum has drawn criticism from left-wing groups. The World Socialist Web Site called it an international organization of counterrevolution serving the region’s most reactionary interests.

Chile’s government, not Kast himself, publicly defended his participation. Social Development Minister Maria Jesus Wulf said Kast had helped found the forum and had every right to keep attending.

Logistics and Schedule

Milei’s schedule was tight: he arrived in Santiago in the morning, spoke at the forum, and then had meetings at La Moneda. His return flight left Santiago at 13:30, arriving in Argentina at 15:30.

The quick turnaround shows the importance he places on regional alliances. The visit lasted only a few hours.

The Madrid Charter and Fundación Disenso

The Madrid Charter is a document that outlines conservative principles, signed by right-wing politicians across the Spanish-speaking world. Fundación Disenso, linked to Vox, promotes these ideas through forums and events.

Kast was an original signatory of the charter, making him a key figure in this network. The forum in Santiago is part of a series of regional meetings to expand this influence.

What the Meeting Means

The meeting between Milei and Kast signals a strengthening of the right-wing axis in South America. Both leaders share similar views on economics and migration.

Observers note that such meetings could lead to closer cooperation on security and trade. However, no concrete outcomes were announced.

Regional Context

The forum comes at a time when right-wing leaders are gaining ground in several Latin American countries. Milei‘s visit to Chile is part of this broader trend.

The event also serves as a platform for these leaders to coordinate strategies. The presence of U.S. official Sarah Rogers indicates international interest.

No Major Announcements

Despite the high-profile meeting, no major agreements were signed or announced. The focus was on dialogue and building relationships.

Milei’s quick return to Argentina suggests the visit was more symbolic than substantive. The two presidents discussed shared agendas on foreign relations, migration control, and regional security, according to reports.

Looking Ahead

The meeting sets the stage for future cooperation between Argentina and Chile under conservative leadership. Both countries face similar challenges, including economic instability and migration pressures.

The Madrid Forum’s next regional meeting is expected to continue this dialogue. For now, the visit marks another step in Milei’s efforts to build alliances abroad.

Event Scale and Reach

The Madrid Forum’s fifth regional meeting in Santiago on 3 and 4 September 2026 brought together over 40 speakers from 25 countries. Chile’s Emol newspaper reported this on 28 August 2026.

This made it one of the largest conservative and far-right leader gatherings in Latin America that year. Its slogan was ‘A new era for Ibero-America.’

Fundación Disenso, a think tank linked to Spain’s Vox party, organized the event. It took place at Santiago’s Centro de Eventos San Carlos de Apoquindo.

Pre-Existing Tensions

The visit occurred during separate tension over the Cerimedo affair and the Magellan Strait. Argentine and Chilean outlets covered both stories through late August 2026.

On 29 August 2026, The Clinic reported the bilateral meeting would be ‘marked by the recent incident around the Strait of Magellan.’ This referred to diplomatic friction between Argentina and Chile.

These issues were not part of the public agenda for the forum but framed the context of the leaders’ discussions.

Meeting Logistics and Schedule

Milei’s flight left Buenos Aires at 07:00 on 3 September 2026, per Infobae. It was scheduled to return at 13:30, arriving in Argentina at 15:30.

He spoke at the forum at 09:30, then went to La Moneda to meet the State Department official.

The bilateral meeting with Kast followed around midday. No outlet gave an exact time for the Rogers meeting itself.

Previous Encounters and Future Steps

El Cronista reported that the Santiago bilateral would be their fourth face-to-face meeting since Kast’s runoff win in December 2025. It listed a Buenos Aires meeting, Kast’s March inauguration and an April visit as the earlier three.

This indicated an ongoing relationship between the two leaders, who had met previously in other contexts.

No major announcements or agreements were reported from the meeting. The visit ended with Milei’s return to Argentina that same day, per Infobae’s schedule.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the Madrid Forum?

The Madrid Forum is a right-wing political meeting organized by Fundación Disenso, a think tank linked to Spain’s Vox party. It brings together conservative leaders from Europe and the Americas.

Why did Milei visit Chile?

Milei visited Chile to speak at the Madrid Forum and hold a bilateral meeting with President José Antonio Kast. The trip aimed to strengthen ties between the two conservative governments.

What is the Madrid Charter?

The Madrid Charter is a document promoting conservative values, signed by right-wing politicians. José Antonio Kast was an original signatory.

Did Milei and Kast sign any agreements?

No specific agreements were announced during the meeting. The talks focused on regional issues and bilateral relations.

Sources: Infobae; Emol; La Tercera; El Mostrador; The Clinic; Cadena 3; Política Viral; Ex-Ante; WSWS.

World.title: ‘In A Tight Spot’: Woman gets 4 months in jail after police find crack pipe stashed in her butt crack
World.content:
‘In A Tight Spot’: Woman gets 4 months in jail after police find crack pipe stashed in her butt crack

By Breaking Belize News Staff: Police officers found themselves in a sticky situation, and a Belize City woman found herself in a tight spot after hiding a crack pipe in the crack of her buttocks when officers approached her. And because she has multiple prior convictions, she has been sentenced to four months in prison.

Leiyana Louise Whylie, 30, a cleaner of Tigris Street, appeared in the Belize City Magistrate’s Court on Thursday, where she pleaded guilty to possession of a utensil used for smoking a controlled drug.

Police say Whylie was busted at about 8:30 a.m. on Wednesday, September 2, while officers were conducting mobile patrols on Tigris Street.

According to police, an officer saw Whylie sitting in a chair and observed her push something behind her back as officers approached.

During a subsequent search for illegal drugs, firearms and ammunition, the officer reportedly felt a hard object in the rear portion of Whylie’s underwear. Further checks revealed a silver metal crack pipe lodged in the crack of her buttocks, police say.

Whylie pleaded guilty and asked the court to impose a fine.

In mitigation, she told the court, “I know dah wah charge but I recently got a job. Everyday I try do better than before.”

The Magistrate, however, noted Whylie’s previous drug-related convictions, including prior convictions involving crack pipes, and said another non-custodial sentence would not be appropriate.

She was sentenced to three months in prison for the latest offence.

Whylie also had an outstanding $805 fine dating back to July 25, 2024, which carried a default sentence of four months in prison. Both sentences were ordered to run concurrently, meaning she will serve a total of four months at the Belize Central Prison.

Whylie also indicated that she intends to enroll in a drug rehabilitation programme while incarcerated.

World.title: Government of Belize launches National Commission for Persons with Disabilities
World.content:
Government of Belize launches National Commission for Persons with Disabilities

By Zoila Palma: Today, the Government of Belize, through the Ministry of Human Development, Family Support and Gender Affairs launched the National Commission for Persons with Disabilities.

The National Commission is the principal body responsible for promoting and monitoring the rights of persons with disabilities, while advising policymakers on their effective implementation across Belize.

In 2024, GOB enacted the Disabilities Act, a landmark piece of legislation affirming the rights of persons with disabilities to equal treatment, accessibility, and full participation in national life.

“Today’s ceremony is a defining moment in the country’s journey toward a society where every citizen can contribute and thrive without barriers. This Commission will act as the bridge between Government, civil society, and Belizeans living with disabilities,” the Ministry said.

World.title: Belize@45 Youth Summit to inspire ideas for Belize’s future
World.content:
Belize@45 Youth Summit to inspire ideas for Belize’s future

By Zoila Palma: The National Celebrations Commission is preparing to host the fifth annual Belize Creative Youth Ideas Summit, providing young Belizeans with a platform to share their perspectives and present bold ideas for the country’s future.

Through the theme Belize@45, the summit will bring young people together to collaboratively explore a key question: If Belize is 45 today, what should Belize look like five years from now at Belize@50? The initiative aims to encourage creativity, innovation and youth participation in shaping the nation’s development.

The Belize@45 Creative Youth Ideas Summit will take place on September 8, 2026, creating an interactive space for young Belizeans to imagine the Belize they want to build.

World.title: Belize Sports Summit 2026 highlights future of Sports!
World.content:
Belize Sports Summit 2026 highlights future of Sports!

By Zoila Palma: Day Two of the Belize Sports Summit 2026 today, focused on the future of sports in Belize, with discussions centered on the role of sports in transforming individuals, communities and the wider country.

Minister of State for Youth and Sports, Devin Daly, opened the day by examining the trajectory of sports development in Belize while encouraging young people to take advantage of the opportunities available to them.

The morning program also featured a Signature Session by the President of the Belize Olympic and Commonwealth Games Association, along with presentations from PANAM Sports on sports development across the region.

The sessions highlighted opportunities for Belize to strengthen its sporting sector and further integrate with regional and international sports development initiatives.

The morning concluded with a panel discussion on “Sports Tourism, Diaspora Engagement and Regional Opportunity,” moderated by Director of Tourism Evan Tillett.

The discussion explored the potential for sports to support tourism, strengthen engagement with the Belizean diaspora and create new regional opportunities, followed by a question-and-answer session that allowed attendees to engage directly with the panelists.

World.title: Mayor Earl Trapp: Santa Elena to inaugurate 1st ever synthetic field
World.content:
Mayor Earl Trapp: Santa Elena to inaugurate 1st ever synthetic field

By Zoila Palma: The San Ignacio and Santa Elena Town Council is continuing its infrastructure development efforts across the municipality, Mayor Earl Trapp said.

The Mayor says that Requena Street in Santa Elena, behind the Complex, is currently undergoing upgrading works as part of the council’s ongoing efforts to improve local infrastructure.

In addition, the Joseph Andrews Park and Santa Elena’s own synthetic turf are nearing inauguration, providing an improved sporting facility aimed at encouraging children and youths to participate in sports and other activities.

Mayor Trapp said the council remains committed to improving the quality of life for residents while promoting a cleaner, healthier and more developed municipality.

World.title: Investing in healthcare: $2.5 million scholarship program supports 67 Belizeans
World.content:
Investing in healthcare: $2.5 million scholarship program supports 67 Belizeans

By Zoila Palma: Sixty-seven Belizeans pursuing higher education in health-related fields have been awarded scholarships through a collaboration between the Ministry of Health and Wellness, Ministry of Education, Culture, Science and Technology, the Inter-American Development Bank (IDB) and several tertiary-level institutions.

The scholarship recipients, who have signed bonds with the Government of Belize, will receive financial support throughout their programs, allowing them to focus on their studies. Areas of study include nursing, medicine, mental health and biomedical engineering.

The initiative is aimed at strengthening Belize’s public healthcare system by developing and retaining highly skilled professionals.

The program also seeks to empower scholarship recipients to expand their expertise and contribute to improving the health and well-being of Belizeans.

With a BZ$2.5 million investment this year, the scholarship program represents a significant commitment to building a stronger healthcare workforce and preparing the next generation of professionals to meet Belize’s evolving health needs.

World.title: International News: France records hottest summer ever as heatwaves, drought and wildfires intensify
World.content:
International News: France records hottest summer ever as heatwaves, drought and wildfires intensify

By Zoila Palma: France experienced its hottest summer on record in 2026, with extreme heat, drought and widespread wildfires affecting the country, Environment Minister Monique Barbut said today.

The record was set during the June-to-August meteorological summer, France 24 reports.

France endured multiple severe heatwaves, including one in late June that set a new intensity record and another that lasted 23 days, tying the country’s longest heatwave record previously established in 1983.

Meteo-France reported 53 days of heatwave conditions during the summer, describing the figure as unprecedented.

The extreme weather also fueled a major wildfire season, with forests suffering extensive damage. Barbut said that by the end of August, fires had burned six times more land than the average recorded over the previous 20 years.

Heatwaves across Europe also contributed to thousands of excess deaths in France, while schools were closed and residents struggled to cope with soaring temperatures.

World.title: International News: Canada ready for US trade deal to benefit both countries
World.content:
International News: Canada ready for US trade deal to benefit both countries

By Zoila Palma: Today, Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said that Canada is prepared to sign a trade agreement with the United States, provided it delivers benefits to both countries and offers stability and credibility for workers, families and businesses.

Speaking in Thunder Bay, Ontario, Carney said Canada is ready to return to negotiations when Washington is prepared to do so.

Carney rejected claims by US Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent that Canada abandoned trade talks because of domestic political considerations.

He also said the US position appears to have softened on several issues since negotiations broke down last month, including concerns over Canadian language and culture.

The latest developments come as tensions remain between the two countries over trade.

Shortly after Carney’s remarks, US President Donald Trump criticized the Canadian prime minister in a Truth Social post, accusing Carney of portraying him as an enemy and warning that such an approach could have severe consequences for Canada’s economy.

World.title: UPDATE: Robert Morgan orders investigation into MoBay perimeter road death
World.content:
A police vehicle at the scene where a engineer died while died while working on a section of the Montego Bay bypass.

KINGSTON, Jamaica — Minister with Responsibility for Works Robert Morgan says he is deeply saddened and has ordered an investigation following the death of a supervising engineer at the Montego Bay Perimeter Road Project on Thursday.

“On behalf of the Government, the ministry and our implementing agencies, I extend sincere condolences to the family, loved ones and colleagues of the deceased. We share their grief at this profoundly difficult time,” said Morgan.

The statement comes hours after the engineer died from injuries he sustained after being run over by a truck while carrying out his duties along a section of the roadway, also referred to as the Montego Bay bypass in St James.

READ: Engineer dies after being crushed by truck while working on MoBay bypass

In acknowledging the incident, Morgan said an investigation has been opened.

“I have directed that a thorough investigation be conducted into the circumstances surrounding the incident. The contractor, China Harbour Engineering Company (CHEC), is required to cooperate fully with all relevant authorities and ensure that the facts are established promptly and transparently.

He expressed deep regret at the death of the engineer.

“A tragedy of this nature should never occur on any of our worksites. No deadline, project target or operational consideration is more important than the safety and life of a worker,” he stressed

“The protection of every person working on our infrastructure projects is non-negotiable. We remain resolute in our commitment of ensuring the safety of every worker,” Morgan concluded.

World.title: Crisis in the classrooms
World.content:
The 2026 Global School-Based Student Health Survey has painted an alarming picture of the state of Jamaican children surveyed with the data showing “an increase in suicidal ideation and attempts” by students in grades nine to 11 with girls outstripping boys in both thinking about the act and attempting it.

According to researchers, in comparing the 2010, 2017 and 2026 survey results, “mental health indicators have worsened over time with more students reporting suicidal thoughts, suicidal planning, suicide attempts, anxiety and depression”.

With a sample size of 3,058 students between grades 7 and 12 the survey administered questionnaires where the children were quizzed on their behaviours over the past seven days, the past 30 days, and the past 12 months.

The study, which was officially released on Wednesday morning by Health Minister Dr Christopher Tufton in collaboration with representatives of the National Council on Drug Abuse, found that suicidal thoughts were highest among grade 11 students with 36.6 per cent of girls saying they had thought about killing themselves as against 23.1 per cent of boys.

Chillingly it said, 32.4 per cent of grade nine girls, 21.8 per cent of grade eight boys, and 21.5 per cent of grade ten boys reported that they attempted to end their lives since this year.

In the meantime anxiety was highest among grade 10 girls with 46.2 per cent experiencing this, and 16.8 per cent of their grade 11 male peers.

Girls again led the way in reporting depression, with the highest numbers being among grade 11 students where 47.8 per cent of girls and 23.8 per cent of boys said they experienced this.

According to the experts, “If current trends persist, several critical challenges threaten adolescent well-being” across three primary areas.

“First, rising adolescent mental health crises involve escalating rates of emotional distress, feelings of hopelessness and self-harm risk indicating that early action matters,” the experts said.

Secondly they said, “Untreated distress negatively affects school engagement, interpersonal relationships, and substance use risks, demonstrating that untreated problems today lead to greater harm tomorrow”.

“Third, stigma and limited services delay professional help-seeking due to barriers like social judgement, restricted access and long wait times emphasising that early support saves lives” the experts said.

According to researchers, to address the issues several questions must be raised including about the extent to which school-based mental health initiatives address early screening and timely referrals, the clarity of suicide prevention pathways between home, school and community and the impact and scope of the expansion of access to adolescent mental health services.

In the meantime an assessment of social media use and screen time found that “most students have a mobile phone and use it for online activities”. According to the data 87.4 per cent of students surveyed have a mobile phone, 77.5 per cent use their devices for social media/online communication or Internet browsing, while 67. 2 per cent spend three-plus hours of screen time on an average school day. Interestingly, only 39 per cent said their parents or guardians have rules about social media use.

The researchers, in noting that the “high levels of screen time highlight the importance of digital balance and supportive rules” said this was so as “excessive screen time can impact physical, social and mental health”.

In addition they warned that excessive social media use can affect relationships and in-person interactions, and also “increases exposure to risky content and online pressures”.

“If current trends persist, several digital-related challenges emerge across multiple areas. First, there is reduced sleep, activity and family engagement as screen time displaces healthy habits,” the canvasser said, while noting that individuals experience greater exposure to online harms and social pressures, including negative comments, fake news and unrealistic comparisons.

“Thirdly, widening gaps in parental digital supervision appear between technologically confident families who maintain open conversations, privacy settings and screen time limits and parents lacking knowledge or time who are unfamiliar with risks, unclear about settings or have little time to monitor,” the experts declared.

They said to guide future efforts the extent to which health digital habits are promoted in schools must be determined.

In addition the experts said the parenting initiatives in existence for social media provision and monitoring must be known as well as the way in which cyberbullying, online exploitation and harmful content are built into adolescent mental health services.

The GSHS is an international gold-standard survey developed by World Health Organization, in collaboration with United Nations Children’s Fund; United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization; United States Agency for International Development; and the United States-based Centers for Disease Control and Prevention.

It measures self-reported health behaviours and protective factors among youth 13-17 years old in the area of alcohol, tobacco and drug use, dietary behaviour, physical activity, sexual behaviours, violence and unintentional injury and protective factors.

It also establishes trends, and facilitates international comparison, develops priorities, establishes programmes, facilitates resource advocacy for school and youth health programmes/policies.

World.title: Minister cites importance of review process in school repairs
World.content:
The entrance to Ferris Primary School in Westmoreland showing buildings to the left and back that received new roofs. Repair work is left to be carried out on the administrative block to the right. (Photo: Anthony Lewis)

FERRIS, Westmoreland — The importance of speed and having a review process are among the lessons education minister Senator Dr Dana Morris Dixon is taking from the less-than-smooth process of repairing more than 300 schools damaged by last year’s Hurricane Melissa.

“With our contractors, you have to have multiple entities that are reviewing. There are multiple stages of review. I think we’ve also learned how to do it quicker. Because, remember, it’s 300 contracts with 300 different scopes of work. And you’re going to need to have the quantity surveyors doing their work for 300 different contracts. It’s a lot, but I do think that going through this, it will make it much easier as we’re doing projects going forward because we’re not going to be in a position to do this many [schools] again. And so we’ve really built that muscle memory to be able to do this better going forward,” stated Morris Dixon, who also spoke about steps taken to ensure buildings can cope better with future storms.

The minister was responding to queries from the Jamaica Observer while fielding questions from the media at Ferris Primary School in Westmoreland following a tour of schools in the parish on Wednesday. The other institutions visited were Maud McLeod High and Beaufort Primary schools, both located in Darliston.

Describing the undertaking as unprecedented, Morris Dixon again conceded that fixing the damage left by last October’s Hurricane Melissa had been a challenge.

“It was a big undertaking; it’s something that we’ve never done in our history, you know, this kind of scale of repair of our schools and then doing it in terms of resilience. That is a big task, a very difficult task, under very difficult conditions. There were areas that didn’t work as well as we wanted, and then some things went really smoothly,” she said.

“It was a mixed bag but the team at NET (National Education Trust) has been very focused on reviewing what’s out there, the contracts, and making sure things are happening. The regions have also been very much a part of it. With all of us working together, I think we’ve been able to iron out a lot of kinks. There were a lot of kinks in the beginning, as you would have in any kind of emergency situation like this, but I think we’ve been able to iron them out,” the minister added.

Meanwhile, as the nation anticipates the reopening of schools for the new term, Morris Dixon assured that all institutions will open next week.

“Based on the report from the regions, every school will be open on Monday. As I said, not all the repairs will be done, but they’ve put in contingency plans. There are some schools that may be on rotation, which is like a shift system. Others will be using tents, some will be using timber structures,” she explained.

While she could not immediately provide the exact number of schools still utilising tents and board structures, she indicated that the targeted time frame to get them off these temporary settings is varied.

“I have schools that need a complete rebuild of some parts of the school. That’s not going to finish this year in some cases; it goes into next year. I have schools where the contractor said, ‘September, end of September, we’ll be finished completely.’ Others, it’s mid-October. So it really depends on the scope of work for the schools. And the schools have been given the timelines within which the work will be finished,” stated Morris Dixon.

At Ferris Primary, Principal Tracie Campbell told the Observer that repair work started in February and they are now 98 per cent ready for orientation on September 7, with classes commencing two days later.

Repairs were completed on the roofs of two buildings and a multi-purpose container. However, work remains to be done on the administrative block, even though the roof remains intact.

“I think we could have finished a while ago. However, since I’m not particularly in that field, I’m not privy to some of the information as to why it would have taken so long. What I do know though is that some of the repairs were not done. They were explaining that it was not in their contract to have it done. Nonetheless, the building officer came, I think it was about last Friday, and so they had other plans as to how to go ahead with fixing or doing the repairs on the remainder of the school,” stated Campbell.

Despite the delays, she expressed satisfaction with the progress.

“I remember when I came first after Melissa and I cried, Minister, because I would have said to myself, ‘It’s like no home, no school’. And to see that we are here and we are coming back… to see my teachers taking pride in fixing up, it’s like a new beginning. It’s a new spark for us. And parents would come in — even last week, parents came — to repaint, to help with the painting,” said Campbell.
